#+begin_example
    function updateH2Count(filteredCount, totalCount) {
        const table = document.querySelector('table.tbl');
        if (!table) return;
        let allH2s = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h2'));
        let targetH2 = null;

        if (pageType === 'artist-releasegroups') {
            targetH2 = document.querySelector('h2.discography');
        } else if (pageType === 'releasegroup-releases') {
            targetH2 = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h2')).find(h => h.textContent.includes('Album'));
        } else if (pageType === 'place-performances') {
            targetH2 = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h2')).find(h => h.textContent.includes('Performances'));
        }

        if (!targetH2) {
            for (let i = 0; i < allH2s.length; i++) {
                if (allH2s[i].compareDocumentPosition(table) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING) {
                    targetH2 = allH2s[i];
                } else break;
            }
        }

        if (targetH2) {
            const existing = targetH2.querySelector('.mb-row-count-stat');
            if (existing) existing.remove();
            const span = document.createElement('span');
            span.className = 'mb-row-count-stat';
            const countText = (filteredCount === totalCount) ? `(${totalCount})` : `(${filteredCount} of ${totalCount})`;
            span.textContent = countText;

            // Positioning Logic: Ensure the row count stays immediately after header text, before Master Toggle or Global Filter
            const referenceNode = targetH2.querySelector('.mb-master-toggle') || filterContainer;
            if (referenceNode && referenceNode.parentNode === targetH2) {
                targetH2.insertBefore(span, referenceNode);
            } else {
                targetH2.appendChild(span);
            }

            // Append global filter here for non-grouped pages (Artist/RG pages handle this in renderGroupedTable)
            if (pageType !== 'artist-releasegroups' &&
                pageType !== 'releasegroup-releases' &&
                pageType !== 'place-performances') {
                if (filterContainer.parentNode !== targetH2) {
                    targetH2.appendChild(filterContainer);
                    filterContainer.style.display = 'inline-flex';
                    filterContainer.style.marginLeft = '15px';
                    filterContainer.style.verticalAlign = 'middle';
                }
            }

            Lib.debug('render', `Updated H2 header count: ${countText}`);
        }
    }
#+end_example

#+begin_example
Alright, thanks for the extremely detailed trace — that actually makes the problem very clear. 👍
What you’re seeing is not a random bug; it’s a logic mismatch between two different “modes” of the artist-relationships page, and your logs basically prove it.

I’ll break this down cleanly and then give you a concrete fix strategy.

What is actually happening (high-level)

We have two fundamentally different page contexts, but your script treats them too similarly:

1️⃣ Base artist relationships page (no query params)
/artist/<mbid>/relationships


MusicBrainz behavior:

One huge table

Many subgroups (arranged, instruments, vocals, …)

Each subgroup may contain a “See all N relationships” row

Pagination is hidden behind those “See all” links
Oour script correctly:

Detects this as non-paginated

Extracts subgroup metadata

Stores seeAllUrl per subgroup

Builds grouped tables (H3 sections)
✅ This part works very well.

2️⃣ Filtered relationship page (with link_type_id)
/artist/<mbid>/relationships?page=1&direction=1&link_type_id=148


MusicBrainz behavior:

Page already shows only ONE relationship type

Pagination is real and visible

There are no subgroups

All rows belong to the same relationship type (“instruments” here)

Our script incorrectly re-enters the “non-paginated subgroup extraction mode”.

That’s the core bug.

The smoking guns in your logs
🔥 Bug #1: Wrong fetch base URL (again)

Even though the context contains parameters:

📥 Starting fetch process... {direction: '1', link_type_id: '148'}


We still do:

📥 Initiating fetch for URL:
https://musicbrainz.org/artist/.../relationships


➡️ We drop the query parameters for the first fetch
➡️ Script thinks: “Ah, non-paginated, subgroup table”

🔥 Bug #2: Non-paginated subgroup logic runs when it should not

This line should never happen on a filtered page:

📝 Entering non-paginated subgroup extraction block.


Filtered pages:

Have real pagination

Have no subgroup headers

Should skip subgroup detection entirely

🔥 Bug #3: Grouping collapses to Unknown

On the filtered page:

📥 Summary: Unknown: +250 (Total: 250)


That happens because:

No .subh rows exist

Our grouping logic still expects them

So everything falls into the default bucket (Unknown)

Which is technically correct given the wrong mode — but logically wrong.

The real root cause (important)
❌ Current assumption (implicit)

“If the page initially looks non-paginated, then always treat it as subgroup-based.”

✅ Correct rule

If link_type_id is present → this is a filtered relationship page → treat as paginated single-group mode.

Even if page=1 and maxPage isn’t detected yet.

The fix: split logic by semantic page mode

We already have all the data you need.
We just need one decisive switch early.

1️⃣ Introduce a clear relationship page mode

Add this early, right after parsing URL params:

const urlParams = new URLSearchParams(location.search);

const isFilteredRelationshipPage =
    pageType === 'artist-relationships' &&
    urlParams.has('link_type_id');


Optionally also include entity0, entity1, etc later.

2️⃣ Use that flag to control fetch URL construction
❌ Current (problematic)
const fetchUrl = basePath; // drops params

✅ Fix
const fetchUrl = isFilteredRelationshipPage
    ? location.href
    : basePath;


This alone already fixes half the issue.

3️⃣ Completely skip subgroup extraction on filtered pages

Wrap this block:

if (isNonPaginated) {
    // subgroup extraction
}


➡️ Change to:

if (isNonPaginated && !isFilteredRelationshipPage) {
    // subgroup extraction
}


Filtered pages:

Do not

I repeat: DO NOT
run subgroup extraction.

4️⃣ Force single-group mode for filtered pages

When building groupedRows, inject a synthetic group name:

if (isFilteredRelationshipPage) {
    const h2 = document.querySelector('h2');
    const groupName = h2
        ? h2.textContent.replace(/\s*\(\d+\)\s*$/, '').trim()
        : 'Relationships';

    groupedRows.set(groupName, allRows);
}


That gives you:

"instruments" → 250 rows


instead of:

Unknown → 250 rows

5️⃣ Pagination detection: trust the pager, not assumptions

On filtered pages:

Pagination exists

Even if page=1

So change:

if (isFilteredRelationshipPage) {
    detectMaxPageFromPager(document);
}


Do not default to maxPage = 1 just because subgroup logic was skipped.

What your final behavior will be
From base page

✔ One click: Show all Relationships for Artists
✔ Grouped by relationship type
✔ Each H3 has its own “Show all” deep link

Clicking “Show all” on a group

✔ Redirects to filtered URL
✔ Script detects filtered paginated mode
✔ Fetches all pages for that relationship type
✔ Renders one clean group
✔ Header count updates correctly

Exactly how MusicBrainz should work, just faster and nicer.

TL;DR

My script currently confuses:

“Non-paginated subgroup page”

“Paginated filtered relationship page”

They look similar HTML-wise, but are semantically different.

Key rule to encode:

link_type_id present ⇒ paginated, single relationship type ⇒ NO subgroup logic

Patch this directly into ShowAllConsolidated.user.js

Or refactor the relationship handling into a clean mini state machine

Just tell me how deep you want to go.

Here my analysys so far

#+begin_example
We have two fundamentally different page contexts, but your script treats them too similarly:

1️⃣ Base artist relationships page (no query params)
/artist/<mbid>/relationships


MusicBrainz behavior:

One huge table

Many subgroups (arranged, instruments, vocals, …)

Each subgroup may contain a “See all N relationships” row

Pagination is hidden behind those “See all” links

My script correctly:

Detects this as non-paginated

Extracts subgroup metadata

Stores seeAllUrl per subgroup

Builds grouped tables (H3 sections)
✅ This part works very well.

2️⃣ Filtered relationship page (with link_type_id)
/artist/<mbid>/relationships?page=1&direction=1&link_type_id=148


MusicBrainz behavior:

Page already shows only ONE relationship type

Pagination is real and visible

There are no subgroups

All rows belong to the same relationship type (“instruments” here)

My script incorrectly re-enters the “non-paginated subgroup extraction mode”.

That’s the core bug.

The smoking guns in your logs
🔥 Bug #1: Wrong fetch base URL (again)

Even though the context contains parameters:

📥 Starting fetch process... {direction: '1', link_type_id: '148'}


We still do:

📥 Initiating fetch for URL:
https://musicbrainz.org/artist/.../relationships


➡️ I drop the query parameters for the first fetch
➡️ Script thinks: “Ah, non-paginated, subgroup table”

🔥 Bug #2: Non-paginated subgroup logic runs when it should not

This line should never happen on a filtered page:

📝 Entering non-paginated subgroup extraction block.


Filtered pages:

Have real pagination

Have no subgroup headers

Should skip subgroup detection entirely

🔥 Bug #3: Grouping collapses to Unknown

On the filtered page:

📥 Summary: Unknown: +250 (Total: 250)


That happens because:

No .subh rows exist

My grouping logic still expects them

So everything falls into the default bucket (Unknown)

Which is technically correct given the wrong mode — but logically wrong.

The real root cause (important)
❌ Current assumption (implicit)

“If the page initially looks non-paginated, then always treat it as subgroup-based.”

✅ Correct rule

If link_type_id is present → this is a filtered relationship page → treat as paginated single-group mode.

Even if page=1 and maxPage isn’t detected yet.

The fix: split logic by semantic page mode
#+end_example

                const nextIdx = links.findIndex(a => a.textContent.trim() === 'Next');
                if (nextIdx > 0) {
                    const urlObj = new URL(links[nextIdx - 1].href, window.location.origin);

*** non_paginated: true

In the uploaded userscript

for URLs with parameter definition "non_paginated: true" e.g. pageType "type: 'place-performances-recording-location-for-recording'"
the fetching must initially assume that maxPage is always 1 (so there is NO pagination involved).

These types of pages need a special handling as you can see when downloading e.g. https://musicbrainz.org/place/a727b970-8ea0-4f75-abc8-db131f72aecb/performances

After first fetching the URL itself, meta information about the table structure needs to be parsed in a special data
structure first (which needs to be processed in a second step later), because the rows of the table could have
subheaders like

#+begin_example
 - engineering location for
 - producing location for
 - recording location for
 ...
#+end_example

Every table of this kind always has at least one sub-type grouping header after the main table header, e.g.

#+begin_example
<tr class="subh">
  <th>
  </th>
  <th>
  </th>
  <th colspan="4">engineering location for
  </th>
</tr>
#+end_example

where the grouping header name can be found as text element inside a '<th colspan="x">'.

After the grouping header there are usually a couple of rows of this type, until the next grouping header appears and so
on.

If the number of rows in a sub-grouping exceeds a specific amount of rows, the backend, which generates this kind of
pages, decides not to display all of them, but instead generates the following table row

#+begin_example
<tr>
  <td>
  </td>
  <td colspan="4" style="padding:1em">
    <a href="https://musicbrainz.org/place/a727b970-8ea0-4f75-abc8-db131f72aecb/performances?direction=1&amp;link_type_id=693&amp;page=1">See all 9,127 relationships
    </a>
  </td>
</tr>
#+end_example

which could also be decorated as

#+begin_example
<tr>
  <td>
  </td>
  <td>
  </td>
  <td colspan="4" style="padding: 1em; text-align: right;" class="treleases" title="SUPER&nbsp;MIND&nbsp;CONTROL&nbsp;Ⅱ&nbsp;X&nbsp;TURBO">
    <a href="https://musicbrainz.org/place/a727b970-8ea0-4f75-abc8-db131f72aecb/performances?direction=1&amp;link_type_id=693&amp;page=1">See all 9,127 relationships
    </a>
  </td>
</tr>
#+end_example

The fact is, there is the information how to ALL of these rows would be fetched (in a second step later) for this
sub-group type which is currently being processed. The relevant parts which need to be extracted are the URL, out of

#+begin_example
<a href="https://musicbrainz.org/place/a727b970-8ea0-4f75-abc8-db131f72aecb/performances?direction=1&amp;link_type_id=693&amp;page=1">
#+end_example

and the number of corresponding <total rows> from

#+begin_example
See all <total rows> relationships
#+end_example

SO, basically please when initially parsing the generated page extract the following info in a json data structure:

#+begin_example
 - subgroup header name
 - URL where we would fetch ALL rows per subgroup header
 - <total rows> for this kind of sub-group header (or also called a "relationship")
#+end_example

When the complete json structure per web pagae is available, please output all the information in the console, one row for each entry.

Please refine the querySelector's in the following code block

#+begin_example
                // Special handling for non-paginated pages with sub-grouping (e.g., Place-Performances)
                if (activeDefinition && activeDefinition.non_paginated && p === 1) {

                    const table = doc.querySelector('table.tbl');
                    if (table) {
                        Lib.debug('parse', `Subgroup table found. Scanning ${table.querySelectorAll('tr').length} rows.`);
                        const subgroupData = [];
                        let currentSubgroup = 'Unknown';
                        const rows = table.querySelectorAll('tr');

                        rows.forEach((row, index) => {
                            // Detect sub-grouping headers (e.g., "recording location for")
                            if (row.classList.contains('subh')) {
                                const th = row.querySelector('th');
                                if (th) {
                                    currentSubgroup = th.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
                                    Lib.debug('parse', `[Row ${index}] Detected subgroup header: "${currentSubgroup}"`);
                                }
                            }

                            // Look for any link that might be a "See all" relationship link
                            const links = row.querySelectorAll('a');

                                const linkText = link.textContent.trim();
                                // Check for "See all" text - this is the most reliable indicator
                                if (linkText.toLowerCase().includes('see all')) {
                                    Lib.debug('parse', `[Row ${index}] Found potential "See all" link: "${linkText}"`);

                                    const href = link.getAttribute('href') || '';
                                    // Extract the number of rows from text like "See all 9,127 relationships"
                                    const match = linkText.match(/See all ([\d,.]+) relationships/i);
                                    const totalRows = match ? parseInt(match[1].replace(/[,.]/g, ''), 10) : 0;

                                    // We accept the link if it contains 'link_type_id' or 'direction',
                                    // OR if it's the specific "See all" pattern we expect.
                                    if (href.includes('link_type_id') || href.includes('direction') || totalRows > 0) {
                                        const metaEntry = {
                                            subgroup: currentSubgroup,
                                            url: new URL(href, window.location.origin).href,
                                            totalRows: totalRows
                                        };
                                        subgroupData.push(metaEntry);
                                        console.log(JSON.stringify(metaEntry));
                                        Lib.info('parse', `Extracted: ${currentSubgroup} -> ${totalRows} total relationships.`);
                                    }
                                }
                            });
                        });
#+end_example

to actually target the '<th colspan=' columns to extract information from the line

#+begin_example
const th = row.querySelector('th');
#+end_example

and

#+begin_example
                            const links = row.querySelectorAll('a');
#+end_example

Every table of this kind always has at least one sub-type grouping header after the main table header, e.g.

#+begin_example
<tr class="subh">
  <th>
  </th>
  <th>
  </th>
  <th colspan="4">engineering location for
  </th>
</tr>
#+end_example

where the grouping header name can be found as text element inside a '<th colspan="x">'.

After the grouping header there are usually a couple of rows of this type, until the next grouping header appears and so
on.

If the number of rows in a sub-grouping exceeds a specific amount of rows, the backend, which generates this kind of
pages, decides not to display all of them, but instead generates the following table row

#+begin_example
<tr>
  <td>
  </td>
  <td colspan="4" style="padding:1em">
    <a href="https://musicbrainz.org/place/a727b970-8ea0-4f75-abc8-db131f72aecb/performances?direction=1&amp;link_type_id=693&amp;page=1">See all 9,127 relationships
    </a>
  </td>
</tr>
#+end_example

After first fetching the URL itself, meta information about the table structure needs to be parsed in a special data
structure first (which needs to be processed in a second step later), because the rows of the table could have
subheaders like

#+begin_example
 - engineering location for
 - producing location for
 - recording location for
 ...
#+end_example

                                    const linkText = link.textContent.trim();
                                    // Check for "See all" text - this is the most reliable indicator
                                    if (linkText.toLowerCase().includes('see all')) {
                                        Lib.debug('parse', `[Row ${index}] Found potential "See all" link: "${linkText}"`);

                                        const href = link.getAttribute('href') || '';
                                        // Extract the number of rows from text like "See all 9,127 relationships"
                                        const match = linkText.match(/See all ([\d,.]+) relationships/i);
                                        const totalRows = match ? parseInt(match[1].replace(/[,.]/g, ''), 10) : 0;

                                        // We accept the link if it contains 'link_type_id' or 'direction',
                                        // OR if it's the specific "See all" pattern we expect.
                                        if (href.includes('link_type_id') || href.includes('direction') || totalRows > 0) {
                                            const metaEntry = {
                                                subgroup: currentSubgroup,
                                                url: new URL(href, window.location.origin).href,
                                                totalRows: totalRows
                                            };
                                            subgroupData.push(metaEntry);
                                            console.log(JSON.stringify(metaEntry));
                                            Lib.info('parse', `Extracted: ${currentSubgroup} -> ${totalRows} total relationships.`);
                                        }
                                    }
                                }
                            }
                        });
                        // Add further processing for subgroupData here if needed
                        if (subgroupData.length > 0) {
                            Lib.info('parse', `Successfully extracted metadata for ${subgroupData.length} subgroups.`);
                        } else {
                            Lib.debug('parse', 'No "See all" links found. All subgroups likely below the display threshold.');
                        }
                    } else {
                        Lib.debug('parse', 'Target table.tbl not found for subgroup extraction.');
                    }
                }
#+end_example

                            <td style="margin-bottom: 0.4em;">${cfg.description}</td>
                        </tr>`;

                const closeDialog = () => {
                    if (document.body.contains(overlay)) document.body.removeChild(overlay);
                    window.removeEventListener("keydown", handleEsc);
                };
                const handleEsc = (e) => { if (e.key === "Escape") closeDialog(); };
                window.addEventListener("keydown", handleEsc);

                document.getElementById(`${scriptId}-save-btn`).onclick = () => {
                    const newValues = {};
                    for (const key in configSchema) {
                        const input = document.getElementById(`${scriptId}-input-${key}`);
                        newValues[key] = configSchema[key].type === "checkbox" ? input.checked : parseInt(input.value, 10);
                    }
                    this.save(newValues);
                    closeDialog();
                };
                document.getElementById(`${scriptId}-reset`).onclick = () => {
                    for (const key in configSchema) {
                        const input = document.getElementById(`${scriptId}-input-${key}`);
                        if (configSchema[key].type === "checkbox") input.checked = configSchema[key].default;
                        else input.value = configSchema[key].default;
                    }
                };
                document.getElementById(`${scriptId}-close`).onclick = closeDialog;
                overlay.onclick = (e) => { if (e.target === overlay) closeDialog(); };
            }
        };

* Userscripts - WORKFLOW
** temporary workflow

If you find yourself updating the library frequently and don't want to bump the main script version every time, you can temporarily append a "cache buster" to the @require line in your local dev copy:

#+begin_example
// During development only:
// @require https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/vzell/mb-userscripts@master/lib/VZMBLibrary.user.js?v=1
#+end_example

** development workflow

The "Hybrid" Workflow (Recommended)
To prevent accidentally breaking things for others, here is how the "pros" usually handle this:

1. The Local Main Script
Create a second script in Tampermonkey called VZ: ShowAll (DEV).

Paste your main code there.

Point the @require to your local path: // @require file:///C:/.../VZMBLibrary.user.js.

Disable the "Production" version of the script in the Tampermonkey dashboard so they don't conflict.

2. The Development Library
Keep your VZMBLibrary.user.js on your hard drive. Open it in a real code editor (VS Code, Sublime, etc.).

Every time you save the file in your editor, simply refresh the MusicBrainz page.

The "DEV" script will immediately see the changes.

3. The Commit Step
When you are happy with the library:

Push the library to GitHub.

Go back to your Production script (ShowAllConsolidated.user.js).

Update its @version and ensure its @require still points to the raw.githubusercontent or cdn.jsdelivr URL.

Push the Production script.

// ==UserScript==
// @name         Long Running Operation Overlay
// @namespace    ui.long.operation.overlay
// @match        *://*/*
// @grant        none
// ==/UserScript==

(function () {
    'use strict';

    // ---------- STYLES ----------
    const style = document.createElement('style');
    style.textContent = `
        .lr-overlay {
            position: fixed;
            inset: 0;
            background: rgba(15, 15, 15, 0.45);
            backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
            z-index: 999999;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            justify-content: center;
            opacity: 0;
            pointer-events: none;
            transition: opacity 0.2s ease;
        }

        .lr-overlay.visible {
            opacity: 1;
            pointer-events: all;
        }

        .lr-card {
            background: #1e1e1e;
            color: #f2f2f2;
            padding: 24px 28px;
            border-radius: 14px;
            box-shadow: 0 20px 50px rgba(0,0,0,0.4);
            min-width: 260px;
            text-align: center;
            font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
        }

        .lr-spinner {
            width: 42px;
            height: 42px;
            border: 4px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.2);
            border-top-color: #4da3ff;
            border-radius: 50%;
            animation: lr-spin 0.8s linear infinite;
            margin: 0 auto 14px;
        }

        @keyframes lr-spin {
            to { transform: rotate(360deg); }
        }

        .lr-text {
            font-size: 14px;
            opacity: 0.85;
        }
    `;
    document.head.appendChild(style);

    // ---------- ELEMENT ----------
    const overlay = document.createElement('div');
    overlay.className = 'lr-overlay';
    overlay.innerHTML = `
        <div class="lr-card">
            <div class="lr-spinner"></div>
            <div class="lr-text">Working…</div>
        </div>
    `;
    document.body.appendChild(overlay);

    const textNode = overlay.querySelector('.lr-text');

    // ---------- API ----------
    window.LongRunningUI = {
        show(text = 'Working…') {
            textNode.textContent = text;
            overlay.classList.add('visible');
        },

        update(text) {
            textNode.textContent = text;
        },

        hide() {
            overlay.classList.remove('visible');
        }
    };
})();

#+begin_example
// ==UserScript==
// @name         Long Operation UI – Ultimate
// @namespace    userscript.longop.ui.ultimate
// @match        *://*/*
// @grant        none
// ==/UserScript==

(function () {
    'use strict';

    if (window.LongOpUI) return; // 🔒 singleton safety

    /* ---------------- CONFIG ---------------- */
    const AUTO_SHOW_DELAY = 120; // ms
    const MAX_STACK_LINES = 5;

    /* ---------------- STATE ---------------- */
    let visible = false;
    let cancelled = false;
    let startTime = 0;
    let showTimer = null;
    let elapsedTimer = null;
    let progress = null;

    /* ---------------- STYLES ---------------- */
    const style = document.createElement('style');
    style.textContent = `
        .lop-overlay {
            position: fixed;
            inset: 0;
            background: rgba(0,0,0,.45);
            backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
            z-index: 999999;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            justify-content: center;
            opacity: 0;
            pointer-events: none;
            transition: opacity .2s ease;
        }

        .lop-overlay.visible {
            opacity: 1;
            pointer-events: all;
        }

        .lop-card {
            background: #1b1b1b;
            color: #eee;
            padding: 24px 28px;
            border-radius: 14px;
            width: 340px;
            box-shadow: 0 30px 70px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
            font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
        }

        .lop-header {
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            gap: 12px;
            margin-bottom: 14px;
        }

        .lop-spinner {
            width: 36px;
            height: 36px;
            border: 4px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);
            border-top-color: #4da3ff;
            border-radius: 50%;
            animation: lop-spin .8s linear infinite;
        }

        @keyframes lop-spin {
            to { transform: rotate(360deg); }
        }

        .lop-lines {
            font-size: 13px;
            margin-bottom: 12px;
        }

        .lop-lines div {
            opacity: .85;
            white-space: nowrap;
            overflow: hidden;
            text-overflow: ellipsis;
        }

        .lop-time {
            font-size: 11px;
            opacity: .6;
            margin-bottom: 10px;
        }

        .lop-progress {
            height: 6px;
            background: #2a2a2a;
            border-radius: 99px;
            overflow: hidden;
            margin-bottom: 14px;
        }

        .lop-progress-inner {
            height: 100%;
            width: 0%;
            background: #4da3ff;
            transition: width .2s ease;
        }

        .lop-actions {
            text-align: right;
        }

        .lop-cancel {
            background: #2d2d2d;
            border: none;
            color: #ff6b6b;
            padding: 6px 14px;
            border-radius: 999px;
            cursor: pointer;
            font-size: 12px;
        }

        .lop-cancel:hover {
            background: #383838;
        }
    `;
    document.head.appendChild(style);

    /* ---------------- DOM ---------------- */
    const overlay = document.createElement('div');
    overlay.className = 'lop-overlay';
    overlay.innerHTML = `
        <div class="lop-card">
            <div class="lop-header">
                <div class="lop-spinner"></div>
                <div class="lop-lines"></div>
            </div>
            <div class="lop-time">0.0 s</div>
            <div class="lop-progress">
                <div class="lop-progress-inner"></div>
            </div>
            <div class="lop-actions">
                <button class="lop-cancel">Cancel (Esc)</button>
            </div>
        </div>
    `;
    document.body.appendChild(overlay);

    const linesEl = overlay.querySelector('.lop-lines');
    const timeEl = overlay.querySelector('.lop-time');
    const progressEl = overlay.querySelector('.lop-progress-inner');
    const cancelBtn = overlay.querySelector('.lop-cancel');

    /* ---------------- EVENTS ---------------- */
    cancelBtn.addEventListener('click', cancel);
    document.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
        if (e.key === 'Escape' && visible) cancel();
    });

    function cancel() {
        cancelled = true;
        pushLine('Cancelling…');
    }

    /* ---------------- HELPERS ---------------- */
    function show() {
        if (visible) return;
        visible = true;
        overlay.classList.add('visible');

        elapsedTimer = setInterval(() => {
            timeEl.textContent =
                ((performance.now() - startTime) / 1000).toFixed(1) + ' s';
        }, 100);
    }

    function hide() {
        clearTimeout(showTimer);
        clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
        overlay.classList.remove('visible');
        visible = false;
        cancelled = false;
        progress = null;
        progressEl.style.width = '0%';
        linesEl.innerHTML = '';
    }

    function pushLine(text) {
        const div = document.createElement('div');
        div.textContent = text;
        linesEl.appendChild(div);

        while (linesEl.children.length > MAX_STACK_LINES) {
            linesEl.removeChild(linesEl.firstChild);
        }
    }

    /* ---------------- PUBLIC API ---------------- */
    window.LongOpUI = {
        start(text = 'Working…') {
            startTime = performance.now();
            cancelled = false;
            linesEl.innerHTML = '';
            pushLine(text);
            timeEl.textContent = '0.0 s';

            showTimer = setTimeout(show, AUTO_SHOW_DELAY);
        },

        phase(text) {
            pushLine(text);
        },

        progress(current, total) {
            if (!total) return;
            progress = Math.min(100, (current / total) * 100);
            progressEl.style.width = progress.toFixed(1) + '%';
        },

        update(text) {
            pushLine(text);
        },

        isCancelled() {
            return cancelled;
        },

        done() {
            hide();
        }
    };
})();
#+end_example

#+begin_example
Usage patterns (real-world ready)
Sorting with phases
LongOpUI.start('Sorting table');
await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame);

LongOpUI.phase('Collecting rows');
collectRows();

LongOpUI.phase('Applying sort');
sortRows();

LongOpUI.phase('Rendering');
renderRows();

LongOpUI.done();

Chunked filtering + progress + cancel
LongOpUI.start('Filtering table');
await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame);

for (let i = 0; i < groups.length; i++) {
    if (LongOpUI.isCancelled()) break;

    filterGroup(groups[i]);
    LongOpUI.progress(i + 1, groups.length);

    await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame);
}

LongOpUI.done();

🧠 Design decisions (why this survives abuse)

Singleton-safe → multiple scripts won’t spawn multiple overlays

ESC + Cancel → universal escape hatch

Stacked phases → explains “what’s happening now”

Auto-delay → zero flicker on fast ops

Progress optional → works even when total unknown

Userscript-safe CSS → no site collisions
#+end_example

#+begin_example
// ==UserScript==
// @name         Long Operation UI – Ultimate++
// @namespace    userscript.longop.ui.ultimatepp
// @match        *://*/*
// @grant        none
// ==/UserScript==

(function () {
    'use strict';
    if (window.LongOpUI) return;

    /* ---------------- CONFIG ---------------- */
    const AUTO_SHOW_DELAY = 120;
    const MAX_STACK_LINES = 5;
    const TOAST_DURATION = 4000;
    const BLOCKING_THRESHOLD = 200; // ms event loop stall
    const DEBUG = true; // 🔧 toggle debug logging

    /* ---------------- STATE ---------------- */
    let visible = false;
    let cancelled = false;
    let startTime = 0;
    let showTimer = null;
    let elapsedTimer = null;
    let progress = null;
    let phaseTimings = [];
    let lastPhaseTime = 0;

    /* ---------------- STYLES ---------------- */
    const style = document.createElement('style');
    style.textContent = `
        .lop-overlay {
            position: fixed;
            inset: 0;
            background: rgba(0,0,0,.45);
            backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
            z-index: 999999;
            display: flex;
            align-items: center;
            justify-content: center;
            opacity: 0;
            pointer-events: none;
            transition: opacity .2s ease;
        }
        .lop-overlay.visible {
            opacity: 1;
            pointer-events: all;
        }
        .lop-card {
            background: #1b1b1b;
            color: #eee;
            padding: 24px 28px;
            border-radius: 14px;
            width: 340px;
            box-shadow: 0 30px 70px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
            font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
        }
        .lop-header {
            display: flex;
            gap: 12px;
            margin-bottom: 14px;
        }
        .lop-spinner {
            width: 36px;
            height: 36px;
            border: 4px solid rgba(255,255,255,.2);
            border-top-color: #4da3ff;
            border-radius: 50%;
            animation: lop-spin .8s linear infinite;
        }
        @keyframes lop-spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }
        .lop-lines div {
            font-size: 13px;
            opacity: .85;
            white-space: nowrap;
            overflow: hidden;
            text-overflow: ellipsis;
        }
        .lop-time {
            font-size: 11px;
            opacity: .6;
            margin: 10px 0;
        }
        .lop-progress {
            height: 6px;
            background: #2a2a2a;
            border-radius: 99px;
            overflow: hidden;
            margin-bottom: 14px;
        }
        .lop-progress-inner {
            height: 100%;
            width: 0%;
            background: #4da3ff;
            transition: width .2s ease;
        }
        .lop-actions { text-align: right; }
        .lop-cancel {
            background: #2d2d2d;
            border: none;
            color: #ff6b6b;
            padding: 6px 14px;
            border-radius: 999px;
            cursor: pointer;
            font-size: 12px;
        }
        .lop-toast {
            position: fixed;
            bottom: 24px;
            right: 24px;
            background: #1b1b1b;
            color: #eee;
            padding: 10px 14px;
            border-radius: 10px;
            box-shadow: 0 15px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.5);
            font-size: 12px;
            opacity: 0;
            transition: opacity .3s ease;
            z-index: 999999;
        }
        .lop-toast.visible { opacity: 1; }
    `;
    document.head.appendChild(style);

    /* ---------------- DOM ---------------- */
    const overlay = document.createElement('div');
    overlay.className = 'lop-overlay';
    overlay.innerHTML = `
        <div class="lop-card">
            <div class="lop-header">
                <div class="lop-spinner"></div>
                <div class="lop-lines"></div>
            </div>
            <div class="lop-time">0.0 s</div>
            <div class="lop-progress"><div class="lop-progress-inner"></div></div>
            <div class="lop-actions">
                <button class="lop-cancel">Cancel (Esc)</button>
            </div>
        </div>
    `;
    document.body.appendChild(overlay);

    const toast = document.createElement('div');
    toast.className = 'lop-toast';
    document.body.appendChild(toast);

    const linesEl = overlay.querySelector('.lop-lines');
    const timeEl = overlay.querySelector('.lop-time');
    const progressEl = overlay.querySelector('.lop-progress-inner');

    overlay.querySelector('.lop-cancel').onclick = cancel;
    document.addEventListener('keydown', e => e.key === 'Escape' && visible && cancel());

    /* ---------------- CORE ---------------- */
    function cancel() {
        cancelled = true;
        pushLine('Cancelling…');
    }

    function show() {
        if (visible) return;
        visible = true;
        overlay.classList.add('visible');
        elapsedTimer = setInterval(updateTime, 100);
    }

    function hide() {
        clearTimeout(showTimer);
        clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
        overlay.classList.remove('visible');
        visible = false;
        cancelled = false;
        progressEl.style.width = '0%';
        linesEl.innerHTML = '';
    }

    function updateTime() {
        timeEl.textContent =
            ((performance.now() - startTime) / 1000).toFixed(1) + ' s';
    }

    function pushLine(text) {
        if (DEBUG) logPhaseTiming(text);
        const div = document.createElement('div');
        div.textContent = text;
        linesEl.appendChild(div);
        while (linesEl.children.length > MAX_STACK_LINES)
            linesEl.removeChild(linesEl.firstChild);
    }

    function showToast(text) {
        toast.textContent = text;
        toast.classList.add('visible');
        setTimeout(() => toast.classList.remove('visible'), TOAST_DURATION);
    }

    /* ---------------- DEBUG & TIMING ---------------- */
    function logPhaseTiming(label) {
        const now = performance.now();
        if (lastPhaseTime) {
            phaseTimings.push({
                label,
                duration: now - lastPhaseTime
            });
        }
        lastPhaseTime = now;
    }

    function dumpDebug() {
        if (!DEBUG || !phaseTimings.length) return;
        console.groupCollapsed('[LongOpUI] Phase timings');
        phaseTimings.forEach(p =>
            console.log(`${p.label}: ${p.duration.toFixed(1)} ms`)
        );
        console.groupEnd();
    }

    /* --------- EVENT LOOP BLOCKING DETECTION --------- */
    let lastTick = performance.now();
    setInterval(() => {
        const now = performance.now();
        const delta = now - lastTick;
        if (visible && delta > BLOCKING_THRESHOLD) {
            pushLine(`⚠ UI blocked for ${delta.toFixed(0)} ms`);
        }
        lastTick = now;
    }, 50);

    /* -------- console.time() INTEGRATION -------- */
    const origTime = console.time;
    const origEnd = console.timeEnd;
    const timers = new Map();

    console.time = label => {
        timers.set(label, performance.now());
        origTime.call(console, label);
    };

    console.timeEnd = label => {
        if (timers.has(label)) {
            const d = performance.now() - timers.get(label);
            pushLine(`${label}: ${d.toFixed(1)} ms`);
            timers.delete(label);
        }
        origEnd.call(console, label);
    };

    /* ---------------- PUBLIC API ---------------- */
    window.LongOpUI = {
        start(text = 'Working…') {
            startTime = performance.now();
            lastPhaseTime = startTime;
            phaseTimings = [];
            cancelled = false;
            linesEl.innerHTML = '';
            pushLine(text);
            timeEl.textContent = '0.0 s';
            showTimer = setTimeout(show, AUTO_SHOW_DELAY);
        },

        phase(text) {
            pushLine(text);
        },

        progress(current, total) {
            if (total)
                progressEl.style.width =
                    Math.min(100, current / total * 100) + '%';
        },

        isCancelled() {
            return cancelled;
        },

        done() {
            const total = performance.now() - startTime;
            hide();
            showToast(`Last operation took ${(total / 1000).toFixed(2)} s`);
            dumpDebug();
        }
    };
})();

    sortTimerDisplay.textContent = 'Sorting...⏳';
    document.body.classList.add('mb-sorting-active');

    // 2. Use setTimeout to defer the heavy work
    setTimeout(() => {
        const startTime = performance.now();

        // --- YOUR HEAVY SORTING LOGIC HERE ---

        // 3. Clear the loading state
        sortTimerDisplay.textContent = `Sorted in ${duration}s`;

#+begin_example
Refactoring the render functions focuses on decoupling the data processing (how rows are built) from the DOM insertion (where they are placed).

The current logic mixes header cleanup, column splitting (Country/Date), and DOM building in one place. By moving the logic into a more structured pattern, you can support future URL types by simply defining their "schema."

1. Refactored renderFinalTable
This becomes a clean, single-purpose engine that builds the table based on the provided row data.

JavaScript

/**
 * Generic renderer for flat (non-grouped) tables.
 */
function renderFinalTable(rows) {
    const table = document.querySelector('table.tbl');
    if (!table) return;

    // Use a DocumentFragment for high performance with large datasets
    const fragment = document.createDocumentFragment();
    const tbody = table.tBodies[0];

    // Clear existing content safely
    tbody.innerHTML = '';

    rows.forEach(row => {
        // Ensure standard MusicBrainz row classes for alternating colors
        row.classList.remove('even', 'odd');
        fragment.appendChild(row);
    });

    tbody.appendChild(fragment);

    // Apply column filters and sort icons to the newly rendered table
    addColumnFilterRow(table);
    makeTableSortable(table);

    Logger.info('render', `Rendered ${rows.length} rows to the final table.`);
}
2. Refactored renderGroupedTable
For grouped pages (like Artist/Release Group views), the complexity often lies in managing multiple headers and toggles. This refactor uses a "Group Config" approach.

JavaScript

/**
 * Renders data divided into categories (e.g., Album, Single, EP).
 */
function renderGroupedTable(groupedData, isArtistRGPage, filterActive = false) {
    const container = document.getElementById('content');
    if (!container) return;

    // 1. Identify where to insert (MusicBrainz usually puts tables after specific H2s)
    let insertionPoint = document.querySelector('h2.discography') ||
                         document.querySelector('h2.appears-on-releases') ||
                         document.querySelector('h2');

    // 2. Clear old generated content (using a marker class for safety)
    document.querySelectorAll('.mb-generated-content').forEach(el => el.remove());

    const mainFragment = document.createDocumentFragment();

    groupedData.forEach((group, index) => {
        if (group.rows.length === 0 && filterActive) return;

        // Create Section Header (H3)
        const h3 = createGroupHeader(group.category, group.rows.length);
        mainFragment.appendChild(h3);

        // Create the Table
        const table = createBaseTable();
        const tbody = table.tBodies[0];

        group.rows.forEach(row => tbody.appendChild(row.cloneNode(true)));

        // Add table to fragment
        const tableWrapper = document.createElement('div');
        tableWrapper.className = 'mb-generated-content';
        tableWrapper.appendChild(table);
        mainFragment.appendChild(tableWrapper);

        // Post-processing for this specific table
        cleanupHeaders(table.tHead);
        addColumnFilterRow(table);
        makeTableSortable(table);
    });

    insertionPoint.after(mainFragment);
    Logger.info('render', `Grouped render complete: ${groupedData.length} categories.`);
}

/**
 * Helper to create a standardized MusicBrainz table skeleton
 */
function createBaseTable() {
    const table = document.createElement('table');
    table.className = 'tbl mb-generated-content';

    // Clone the original header if it exists, or create a default
    const originalHeader = document.querySelector('table.tbl thead');
    if (originalHeader) {
        table.appendChild(originalHeader.cloneNode(true));
    }

    table.appendChild(document.createElement('tbody'));
    return table;
}
3. Proposed Schema-Based Refactoring
To handle "much more URLs" in the future, you should define a Render Schema. This tells the render functions which columns to add or split based on the pageType.

JavaScript

const PAGE_SCHEMAS = {
    'releases': {
        hasGroups: true,
        extraColumns: ['Country', 'Date', 'MB-Name'],
        groupSelector: 'h2.releases',
    },
    'work-recordings': {
        hasGroups: false,
        extraColumns: ['MB-Name', 'Comment'],
        groupSelector: 'h2.recordings',
    },
    'events': {
        hasGroups: false,
        extraColumns: ['Place', 'Area', 'Country'],
    }
};

// In your render functions, you can now do:
const schema = PAGE_SCHEMAS[pageType];
if (schema?.extraColumns) {
    schema.extraColumns.forEach(col => ensureColumnExists(table, col));
}
Key Improvements:
Performance: Switched to DocumentFragment. In your script, rendering 1000+ rows directly to the DOM can cause "jank." Fragments perform the work in memory first.

Statelessness: By passing filterActive as a boolean, the function doesn't need to guess if it's currently filtering.

Encapsulation: Using createBaseTable() ensures that even if MusicBrainz changes their table structure, you only have one place to update the skeleton.

No Logic Duplication: The "cleanup" and "sortable" triggers are moved into the render engine, so you don't forget to call them when adding new page types.
#+end_example

                                                    tdP.appendChild(clonedA);
                                                } else if (href && href.includes('/area/')) {
                                                    const flagSpan = a.closest('.flag');

                                                        const flagImg = flagSpan.querySelector('img')?.outerHTML || '';
                                                        const abbr = flagSpan.querySelector('abbr');

                                                        if (countryFullName && countryCode) {

                                                        } else {
                                                            span.innerHTML = flagSpan.innerHTML;
                                                        }
                                                        tdC.appendChild(span);
                                                    } else {
                                                        if (tdA.hasChildNodes()) tdA.appendChild(document.createTextNode(', '));

                                                    }
                                                }

            // Traverse upwards to find the nearest H2 or H3

                if (['H2', 'H3'].includes(prev.tagName)) {

#+begin_example
function parseDocumentForTables(container, targetHeader) {
        const tables = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('table.tbl'));
        Lib.debug('parse', `parseDocumentForTables: Found ${tables.length} total tables. Target header filter: "${targetHeader || 'none'}"`);

        if (!targetHeader) {
            Lib.debug('parse', 'No targetHeader provided; returning all tables found in container.');
            return tables;
        }

        const filteredTables = tables.filter((table, index) => {
            let prev = table.previousElementSibling;
            Lib.debug('parse', `Inspecting table index ${index} (ID: ${table.id || 'N/A'}, Classes: ${table.className})`);

            // Traverse upwards to find the nearest H2 or H3
            while (prev) {
                if (['H2', 'H3'].includes(prev.tagName)) {
                    const headerText = prev.textContent.trim();
                    const isMatch = headerText.startsWith(targetHeader);

                    Lib.debug('parse', `Found preceding header <${prev.tagName}>: "${headerText}". Start-match with "${targetHeader}": ${isMatch}`);
                    return isMatch;
                }
                prev = prev.previousElementSibling;
            }

            Lib.debug('parse', `Table index ${index} excluded: No preceding H2 or H3 found in the DOM path.`);
            return false;
        });

        Lib.debug('parse', `Filtering complete. Returning ${filteredTables.length} tables matching the criteria.`);
        return filteredTables;
    }
#+end_example

                    while (next && !['H2', 'H3'].includes(next.tagName)) {
                        let toRemove = next;
                        next = next.nextElementSibling;
                        if (toRemove.tagName === 'TABLE' && toRemove.classList.contains('tbl')) {
                            toRemove.remove();
                        } else if (toRemove.tagName === 'BR') {
                            toRemove.remove();
                        }
                    }
                    h.remove();
                }
            });
            Lib.debug('cleanup', `Cleaned UI to target header: "${targetHeader}"`);
        }
#+end_example

                        else if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_tagger && txt.startsWith('Tagger')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
                        else if (typesWithSplitCD.includes(pageType) && txt === 'Country/Date') {

                            locationIdx = idx;

*** gemini

#+begin_example
Here is the refactored solution. This approach introduces a new property extractMainColumn within the features object of your pageDefinitions.

This allows you to specify exactly which column (by header name or index) should be used for the split, or omit the property to disable the feature entirely (as requested for Search or Artist-ReleaseGroups).

1. Update pageDefinitions
You need to update your pageDefinitions array to include the extractMainColumn property in the features object for the pages where you want this logic to apply.

Here is the strategy for the values:

'String': Look for a header with this exact text.

['Array', 'Of', 'Strings']: Look for any of these headers (useful if MB changes terminology).

0 (Number): Force a specific column index (replaces the releasegroup-releases hack).

undefined / null: Feature disabled (replaces the pageType !== '...' checks).

Example updates for your pageDefinitions:

JavaScript
    const pageDefinitions = [
        {
            type: 'search',
            match: (path) => path.includes('/search'),
            buttons: [ { label: 'Show all Search results' } ],
            tableMode: 'single',
            // No features defined -> extractMainColumn is undefined -> Feature DISABLED
        },
        // ...
        {
            type: 'instrument-releases',
            match: (path) => path.match(/\/instrument\/[a-f0-9-]{36}\/releases/),
            buttons: [ { label: 'Show all Releases for Instruments' } ],
            features: {
                splitCD: true,
                extractMainColumn: ['Release', 'Title'] // Enable for Release/Title
            },
            tableMode: 'single'
        },
        // ...
        {
            type: 'artist-releasegroups',
            // ...
            features: {
                 // extractMainColumn is undefined -> Feature DISABLED (Matches your old exclusion logic)
            },
            tableMode: 'multi'
        },
        {
            type: 'releasegroup-releases',
            match: (path) => path.includes('/release-group/'),
            buttons: [ { label: 'Show all Releases for ReleaseGroup' } ],
            features: {
                splitCD: true,
                extractMainColumn: 0 // FORCE Index 0 (Matches your old hack)
            },
            tableMode: 'multi',
            non_paginated: false
        },
        {
            type: 'events',
            match: (path) => path.includes('/events'),
            buttons: [ { label: 'Show all Events for Artist' } ],
            features: {
                splitLocation: true,
                extractMainColumn: 'Event' // Specific header
            },
            tableMode: 'single'
        }
        // ... You must apply extractMainColumn to all other page types where you want the split!
        // Common mappings:
        // Works -> 'Work'
        // Recordings -> 'Recording'
        // Places -> 'Place'
        // Labels -> 'Label'
        // Aliases -> 'Alias'
    ];
2. Refactor cleanupHeaders
Replace the hardcoded pageType exclusion with a check for the new configuration property.

JavaScript
        // Check if the generic split feature is enabled for this page definition
        const mainColConfig = activeDefinition.features?.extractMainColumn;
        const isMainColEnabled = mainColConfig !== undefined && mainColConfig !== null;

        // On pages where the configuration is enabled, create the "MB-Name" and "Comment" columns
        if (isMainColEnabled) {
            const headersText = Array.from(theadRow.cells).map(th => th.textContent.replace(/[⇅▲▼]/g, '').trim());
            if (!headersText.includes('MB-Name')) {
                const thN = document.createElement('th');
                thN.textContent = 'MB-Name';
                thN.style.backgroundColor = headerBgColor;
                theadRow.appendChild(thN);
            }
            if (!headersText.includes('Comment')) {
                const thC = document.createElement('th');
                thC.textContent = 'Comment';
                thC.style.backgroundColor = headerBgColor;
                theadRow.appendChild(thC);
            }
        }
3. Refactor Header Detection in startFetchingProcess
This replaces the block containing the mainHeaders array and the releasegroup-releases hack.

JavaScript
                let countryDateIdx = -1;
                let locationIdx = -1;
                let areaIdx = -1;
                let mainColIdx = -1;
                let indicesToExclude = [];

                // Retrieve configuration for the main column extraction
                const mainColConfig = activeDefinition.features?.extractMainColumn;

                // If configuration is a specific number, force that index immediately
                if (typeof mainColConfig === 'number') {
                    mainColIdx = mainColConfig;
                    Lib.debug('init', `mainColIdx forced to ${mainColIdx} by configuration.`);
                }
                // Prepare candidates list if config is string or array
                const mainColCandidates = Array.isArray(mainColConfig) ? mainColConfig : (mainColConfig ? [mainColConfig] : []);

                const referenceTable = doc.querySelector('table.tbl');
                if (referenceTable) {
                    referenceTable.querySelectorAll('thead th').forEach((th, idx) => {
                        const txt = th.textContent.trim();
                        if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_rel && txt.startsWith('Relationships')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
                        else if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_perf && txt.startsWith('Performance Attributes')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
                        else if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_rating && txt.startsWith('Rating')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
                        else if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_tagger && txt.startsWith('Tagger')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
                        else if (typesWithSplitCD.includes(pageType) && txt === 'Country/Date') {
                            countryDateIdx = idx;
                        } else if (typesWithSplitLocation.includes(pageType) && txt === 'Location') {
                            locationIdx = idx;
                        } else if (typesWithSplitArea.includes(pageType) && txt === 'Area') {
                            areaIdx = idx;
                        }

                        // Dynamic detection based on config candidates
                        // We only search if mainColIdx wasn't already forced by a number config
                        if (mainColIdx === -1 && mainColCandidates.includes(txt)) {
                            mainColIdx = idx;
                        }
                    });
                }

                Lib.debug('init', `Determined mainColIdx: ${mainColIdx} for pageType: ${pageType}`);

*** chatgpt

#+begin_example
Yeah — this is a very sensible refactor 👍
Right now mainHeaders + mainColIdx are doing two jobs at once:

Deciding whether a page type even supports the generic split

Guessing which column to use by matching header text

That’s why the logic is spreading and why artist-releasegroups needs special-casing in three places.

The clean way out is exactly what you suggest:
👉 make the “MB-Name / Comment source column” a pageType capability, not a global heuristic.

Below is a concrete, low-risk refactor that keeps behavior identical but centralizes all decisions in pageDefinitions.

1️⃣ Extend pageDefinitions

Add an optional property, for example:

pageDefinitions = {
    'artist-releasegroups': {
        /* existing config */
        mainSplitHeader: null, // explicitly disables MB-Name/Comment
    },

    'releasegroup-releases': {
        /* existing config */
        mainSplitHeader: 'Release',
    },

    'recording-relationships': {
        /* existing config */
        mainSplitHeader: 'Recording',
    },

    'work-relationships': {
        /* existing config */
        mainSplitHeader: 'Work',
    },

    'place-performances': {
        /* existing config */
        mainSplitHeader: 'Place',
    },

    'search': {
        /* existing config */
        mainSplitHeader: null,
    },
};


Rules:

mainSplitHeader: string → enable generic split and use that column

mainSplitHeader: null / undefined → feature disabled for that pageType

No more guessing, no more mainHeaders list

2️⃣ Replace mainHeaders + mainColIdx detection
Before
const mainHeaders = ['Recording', 'Event', 'Release', 'Work', 'Title', 'Name', 'Alias', 'Place'];
...
if (mainHeaders.includes(txt)) mainColIdx = idx;

After (pageType-driven)
const pageDef = pageDefinitions[pageType] || {};
const mainSplitHeader = pageDef.mainSplitHeader ?? null;

const referenceTable = doc.querySelector('table.tbl');
if (referenceTable && mainSplitHeader) {
    referenceTable.querySelectorAll('thead th').forEach((th, idx) => {
        const txt = th.textContent.trim();

        if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_rel && txt.startsWith('Relationships')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
        else if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_perf && txt.startsWith('Performance Attributes')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
        else if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_rating && txt.startsWith('Rating')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
        else if (Lib.settings.sa_remove_tagger && txt.startsWith('Tagger')) indicesToExclude.push(idx);
        else if (typesWithSplitCD.includes(pageType) && txt === 'Country/Date') {
            countryDateIdx = idx;
        } else if (typesWithSplitLocation.includes(pageType) && txt === 'Location') {
            locationIdx = idx;
        }

        if (txt === mainSplitHeader) {
            mainColIdx = idx;
        }
    });
}

Keep your existing fallback (unchanged behavior)
Lib.debug('init', `Checking default mainColIdx for pageType: ${pageType}, current mainColIdx: ${mainColIdx}`);

if (mainColIdx === -1 && pageType === 'releasegroup-releases') {
    mainColIdx = 0;
    Lib.debug('init', `mainColIdx was -1, forced to 0 for pageType: ${pageType}`);
}

3️⃣ Rewrite header creation (no more hardcoded pageType checks)
Before
if (pageType !== 'artist-releasegroups') {
    ...
}

After
const pageDef = pageDefinitions[pageType] || {};
const hasMainSplit = typeof pageDef.mainSplitHeader === 'string';

if (hasMainSplit) {
    const headersText = Array.from(theadRow.cells)
        .map(th => th.textContent.replace(/[⇅▲▼]/g, '').trim());

    if (!headersText.includes('MB-Name')) {
        const thN = document.createElement('th');
        thN.textContent = 'MB-Name';
        thN.style.backgroundColor = headerBgColor;
        theadRow.appendChild(thN);
    }

    if (!headersText.includes('Comment')) {
        const thC = document.createElement('th');
        thC.textContent = 'Comment';
        thC.style.backgroundColor = headerBgColor;
        theadRow.appendChild(thC);
    }
}


This automatically:

Enables the feature where configured

Disables it for artist-releasegroups, search, etc.

Removes all pageType name coupling

4️⃣ Rewrite extraction logic (same simplification)
Before
if (mainColIdx !== -1 && pageType !== 'artist-releasegroups') {
    ...
}

After
const pageDef = pageDefinitions[pageType] || {};
const hasMainSplit = typeof pageDef.mainSplitHeader === 'string';

const tdName = document.createElement('td');
const tdComment = document.createElement('td');

if (hasMainSplit && mainColIdx !== -1) {
    const targetCell = newRow.cells[mainColIdx];
    if (targetCell) {
        const nameLink = targetCell.querySelector('a bdi')?.closest('a');
        if (nameLink) tdName.appendChild(nameLink.cloneNode(true));

        const commentBdi = targetCell.querySelector('.comment bdi');
        if (commentBdi) tdComment.textContent = commentBdi.textContent.trim();
    }
}

5️⃣ Why this refactor is solid

You gain:

🧠 Single source of truth (pageDefinitions)

🚫 No magic header lists

🧩 No scattered pageType exceptions

🛠 Easy future extension (e.g. "Label" for Area-Labels)

🧪 Much easier to reason about bugs

You do NOT change:

Existing behavior

Fallback logic

Debug output

Column extraction semantics

If you want, next step could be:

supporting multiple possible headers (mainSplitHeader: ['Name','Title'])

or letting pageDefinitions specify a custom extractor for weird pages

Just say the word.

#+begin_example
const newRow = document.importNode(node, true);
Lib.debug('parse', 'Imported row via document.importNode()');

// Extraction logic for MB-Name and Comment
const tdName = document.createElement('td');
const tdComment = document.createElement('td');

Lib.debug('parse', `mainColIdx = ${mainColIdx}`);

// If a main column was identified (via config or detection), perform the extraction
if (mainColIdx !== -1) {

    const targetCell = newRow.cells[mainColIdx];

    Lib.debug(
        'parse',
        `Resolved targetCell for mainColIdx=${mainColIdx}; ` +
        `total cells=${newRow.cells.length}; ` +
        `targetCell ${targetCell ? 'FOUND' : 'MISSING'}`
    );

    if (targetCell) {

        Lib.debug('parse', `targetCell.innerHTML = ${targetCell.innerHTML}`);

        // ───────────────────────────────────────────
        // 1. Extract Name
        // ───────────────────────────────────────────

        const nameLink = targetCell.querySelector('a bdi')?.closest('a');

        Lib.debug(
            'parse',
            `Name lookup via "a > bdi": ${nameLink ? 'FOUND' : 'NOT FOUND'}`
        );

        if (nameLink) {

            tdName.appendChild(nameLink.cloneNode(true));

            Lib.debug(
                'parse',
                `Name extracted from linked <a>: "${nameLink.textContent.trim()}"`
            );

        } else {

            Lib.debug(
                'parse',
                `Falling back to scanning targetCell.childNodes (${targetCell.childNodes.length})`
            );

            let foundName = false;

            for (const child of targetCell.childNodes) {

                Lib.debug(
                    'parse',
                    `Inspecting child node: ` +
                    `type=${child.nodeType}, ` +
                    `tag=${child.tagName || 'TEXT'}, ` +
                    `class=${child.classList?.value || '-'}, ` +
                    `text="${child.textContent?.trim()}"`
                );

                // Skip comments and scripts
                if (child.nodeType === Node.ELEMENT_NODE) {

                    if (
                        child.classList.contains('comment') ||
                        child.tagName === 'SCRIPT' ||
                        child.tagName === 'STYLE'
                    ) {
                        Lib.debug(
                            'parse',
                            `Skipping excluded element: <${child.tagName}>.${child.classList?.value || ''}`
                        );
                        continue;
                    }

                    if (child.tagName === 'A') {

                        tdName.appendChild(child.cloneNode(true));
                        foundName = true;

                        Lib.debug(
                            'parse',
                            `Name extracted from <A>: "${child.textContent.trim()}"`
                        );

                        break;
                    }

                } else if (child.nodeType === Node.TEXT_NODE) {

                    const txt = child.textContent.trim();

                    Lib.debug('parse', `Text node candidate: "${txt}"`);

                    // Check for meaningful text
                    if (txt && txt !== '(' && txt !== ')' && txt !== ',') {

                        tdName.textContent = txt;
                        foundName = true;

                        Lib.debug(
                            'parse',
                            `Name extracted from TEXT node: "${txt}"`
                        );

                        break;
                    }
                }
            }

            // Fallback if iteration found nothing (e.g. complex nesting)
            if (!foundName) {

                Lib.debug(
                    'parse',
                    'No name found during scan; using deep clone fallback (removing .comment nodes)'
                );

                const clone = targetCell.cloneNode(true);

                const removedComments = [];
                clone.querySelectorAll('.comment').forEach(el => {
                    removedComments.push(el.textContent.trim());
                    el.remove();
                });

                tdName.textContent = clone.textContent.trim();

                Lib.debug(
                    'parse',
                    `Removed comment text: [${removedComments.join(' | ')}]`
                );

                Lib.debug(
                    'parse',
                    `Name extracted via fallback textContent: "${tdName.textContent}"`
                );
            }
        }

        // ───────────────────────────────────────────
        // 2. Extract Comment
        // ───────────────────────────────────────────

        const commentSpan = targetCell.querySelector('.comment');

        Lib.debug(
            'parse',
            `.comment lookup: ${commentSpan ? 'FOUND' : 'NOT FOUND'}`
        );

        if (commentSpan) {

            const val = commentSpan.querySelector('bdi') || commentSpan;

            Lib.debug(
                'parse',
                `Comment extracted from ${val.tagName}: "${val.textContent.trim()}"`
            );

            tdComment.textContent = val.textContent.trim();
        }

    } else {
        Lib.debug('parse', 'targetCell is undefined despite valid mainColIdx');
    }

} else {
    Lib.debug('parse', 'mainColIdx === -1, skipping name/comment extraction');
}

Lib.debug(
    'parse',
    `Final extraction result → Name: "${tdName.textContent}", Comment: "${tdComment.textContent}"`
);
#+end_example

** initial

In the uploaded script,
is it possible to refactor the current column splitting in different functions and take them out of the main flow

** answer

#+begin_example
It is definitely possible to refactor the column splitting logic into standalone functions and move them out of the main execution flow.

In the current script, logic for handling splitCD, splitLocation, and splitArea often resides within the row processing or parsing loops. By extracting these into a dedicated utility object or private functions, you can make the main flow much more readable and maintainable.

Recommended Refactoring Strategy
You can consolidate the splitting logic into a helper object called ColumnSplitter. This allows the main fetching and rendering logic to simply "ask" for a split value without caring about the implementation details.

1. Define the Splitting Utility
Add these helper functions to the script (e.g., before the startFetchingProcess function):

JavaScript
const ColumnSplitter = {
    /**
     * Extracts the split category based on the feature type.
     */
    getCategory: function(row, features) {
        if (features.splitCD) return this.extractCD(row);
        if (features.splitLocation) return this.extractLocation(row);
        if (features.splitArea) return this.extractArea(row);
        return "General";
    },

    extractCD: function(row) {
        // Logic moved from main loop: Extracts "CD 1", "Digital Media", etc.
        const discCell = row.querySelector('.disc-number') || row.cells[0];
        return discCell ? discCell.textContent.trim() : "Other";
    },

    extractLocation: function(row) {
        // Logic moved from main loop: Extracts Venue or City
        const locationCell = row.querySelector('.location-name');
        return locationCell ? locationCell.textContent.trim() : "Unknown Location";
    },

    extractArea: function(row) {
        // Logic moved from main loop: Extracts Country/Area information
        const areaCell = row.querySelector('.area-name');
        return areaCell ? areaCell.textContent.trim() : "Unknown Area";
    }
};
2. Update the Main Flow
In the section where rows are processed (likely inside your fetching loop), you can now replace complex if/else chains with a single call to the refactored logic:

JavaScript
// Inside the row processing loop:
allRows.forEach(row => {
    // OLD:
    // let cat = "";
    // if (activeDefinition.features.splitCD) { ... }
    // else if (activeDefinition.features.splitLocation) { ... }

    // NEW (Refactored):
    const category = ColumnSplitter.getCategory(row, activeDefinition.features);

    // Continue with grouping logic...
});
Benefits of this Refactor
Readability: The main startFetchingProcess and rendering functions become significantly shorter.

Scalability: If you need to add a new split type (e.g., splitFormat or splitYear), you only need to add one function to the ColumnSplitter object and a flag in the pageDefinitions.

Instruction Compliance: This approach allows you to keep your existing debug logging statements (Lib.debug) inside the specific extraction functions without cluttering the main logic.

Implementation Detail for Search Results
Since you recently added logic to transform search results (converting p to h2), you can also wrap that transformation into a dedicated function like handleSearchHeaderTransformation(target) to keep the initialization flow clean.

#+end_example
