"is it normal that it takes about 7 seconds for the 'Columnsize measuring time'"

1. Why it takes so long — and why 7s is optimistic
The row you pasted contains several expensive-to-measure elements:
Rating stars column — 5 <a> elements each with a ~200-character href containing a full returnto= URL. When cloned into measureDiv and offsetWidth is read, the browser must resolve the full inline layout of all 5 anchors. For 4364 rows that's 21,820 anchor elements measured.
Location column — a <li> with 4 nested <a> elements, area names, a flag <span> with a CSS icon (requires icon font metrics), and <bdi> elements with Unicode text. The ul > li measurement loop clones and measures each li individually on top of the cell measurement.
Event name column — <bdi> wrapping a long Unicode string with date separators (‐ U+2010, not ASCII hyphen). bdi elements trigger bidirectional text resolution which is expensive.
The root cost: every offsetWidth read forces a synchronous full-page reflow. The measurement div is attached to document.body, so the browser must lay out the entire live page — 4364 rendered rows, sidebar, navigation — to answer each offsetWidth query. For 4364 rows × 8 columns × multiple li items = potentially 50,000+ forced reflows. At even 5ms each that's 250 seconds.
The 451s → 375s → 323s numbers are not a bug — they are expected behaviour for the current implementation on this page type.

2. Why repeat access is faster — three compounding reasons
Reason 1: Font metrics cache (biggest factor)
The first offsetWidth read involving the flag icon font (flag-US CSS class), the MusicBrainz rating star CSS, and any custom web fonts triggers a font load + metric computation. The browser must download the font file, parse it, and compute glyph metrics before it can answer the layout query. On first access this blocks each measurement. On second and third access the font metrics are in memory — the measurement starts immediately.
The flag column alone — one icon font loaded once — likely accounts for 30–60 seconds of the first-access cost.
Reason 2: CSS specificity and computed style cache
getComputedStyle() (called implicitly during layout) must resolve the full CSS cascade for each cloned element on first access. MusicBrainz has a large stylesheet. After the first pass the browser's style engine has cached the computed values for the element patterns it has seen. Clones of similar elements resolve faster on subsequent passes.
Reason 3: V8 JIT compilation
The measurement loop runs tens of thousands of iterations. On first run V8 interprets the bytecode. By the second or third run the hot path is JIT-compiled to native code. The JavaScript execution cost drops significantly — not the dominant factor here but contributes to the trend.

The fix that actually solves this
The chunked async approach discussed earlier prevents the Chrome unresponsive dialog and adds progress feedback, but it doesn't reduce the total measurement time — it just spreads the same work across frames.
To actually make measurement fast, the offsetWidth-per-cell approach needs to change. The correct approach is:
Measure once per unique content pattern using a detached offscreen container:
javascript// Create a hidden table OUTSIDE the live DOM — position:absolute, left:-9999px
// Append ALL cells to measure in one batch
// Read ALL offsetWidths in one pass (single reflow)
// Remove the container
Currently the measurement container is created and destroyed per table, but the offsetWidth is read per cell while the container is attached to document.body. Each read triggers a full reflow of the live page.
The fix: collect all cells to measure into a single detached <table> structure, attach it once to a position:fixed; visibility:hidden container outside the viewport, read all offsetWidth values in a tight loop (browser batches these into a single reflow since the live DOM hasn't changed between reads), then detach the container.
This reduces 50,000 forced reflows to one — or at worst one per chunk if chunking is preserved for progress feedback. Expected improvement: 50–100× — bringing a 375-second operation down to 4–8 seconds regardless of page revisit count.
This is a more substantial change to toggleAutoResizeColumns than the progress indicator alone, but the two changes naturally go together in the P3 session.You said: what performance gain in seconds could I expect for the above example of 4100 rows - initially Auto-resized 20 visible columns in 451285ms with this changewhat performance gain in seconds could I expect for the above example of 4100 rows - initially Auto-resized 20 visible columns in 451285ms with this change2:18 PMClaude responded: Let me reason through this carefully with the actual row structure you provided.Let me reason through this carefully with the actual row structure you provided.

Why the current cost is 451 seconds
For 4364 rows × 20 columns the current code does roughly:

One offsetWidth read per cell = ~87,000 reads
One offsetWidth read per ul > li item — your location column has 1 li with nested spans, rating column has no li = ~4,000–8,000 additional reads
Each read attached to document.body = full live-page reflow each time
Live page has 4364 rendered rows, sidebar, navigation = expensive reflow

At ~5ms per forced reflow on a mid-range machine: 95,000 × 5ms = 475 seconds. Matches your observed 451s closely.

What the single-reflow approach changes
Instead of 95,000 individual reflows you get:
Phase 1 — build detached measurement table (zero reflows)
Clone all cells into an offscreen <table> in a position:fixed; visibility:hidden; left:-9999px container. Pure DOM construction, no layout queries. Cost: proportional to clone speed only — roughly 0.1ms per cell = ~10 seconds for 87,000 cells.
Wait — that's still slow. The cloning itself at scale is expensive.
The real optimisation: measure headers only, not every cell
For column width purposes you don't actually need to measure every cell. You need the widest cell per column. The current code finds this by measuring all cells. But a smarter approach:

Measure all cells in the first 50–100 rows (captures typical content width)
Measure all header cells (always needed)
For columns containing variable-length content (title, location), scan all rows but only read textContent.length to find the longest string, then measure only that cell

This reduces 87,000 measurements to roughly 2,000–3,000.
But even the naive single-reflow approach is much faster:
Batch all cells into one detached container → one offsetWidth burst → browser does one layout pass on a small offscreen table (no sidebar, no 4364 live rows) instead of 95,000 layouts on the full page.
Reflow cost of a small offscreen table: ~0.05ms vs ~5ms for the live page = 100× cheaper per read.
95,000 × 0.05ms = 4.75 seconds

Realistic expected times
ApproachExpected timevs currentCurrent (per-cell, live DOM reflow)375–451s1×Chunked async only (no reflow fix)375–451ssame (just non-blocking)Single offscreen reflow, all cells4–8s~60–80× fasterSingle offscreen reflow, smart sampling (first 100 rows + longest)0.5–1.5s~400× fasterSingle offscreen reflow, headers + longest string only0.1–0.3s~1500× faster

Honest caveats
The 4–8s estimate for the naive single-reflow approach depends on:

Whether the browser truly batches all reads in one layout pass on a detached table (it should, but browser implementations vary)
Clone cost — 87,000 deep cell clones still takes time even without layout
Your specific machine — the 5ms → 0.05ms ratio is typical but not guaranteed

The smart sampling approach (first 100 rows + longest text per column) has one risk: if the widest cell is not in the first 100 rows and not the longest text string (e.g. a cell with a short text but a wide embedded icon), the column could be slightly underestimated. For most MusicBrainz columns this is safe. For the rating column (fixed-width star icons regardless of text) you'd always just measure one cell.
The flag icon font was identified as a major first-access cost. Even with single-reflow measurement, the first page visit pays the font-load cost. Subsequent visits remain fast either way.

What to implement in P3
Given the numbers, the right P3 implementation is:

Smart sampling — measure all header cells + first 100 rows + the single longest-text cell per column
Single offscreen container — one detached table, all measurements batched, one reflow
Chunked progress display — still useful for the first 100-row sample pass and gives visual feedback even if total time drops to 1–2 seconds
Return resize duration — append to globalStatusDisplay as discussed

Expected result for your 4364-row table: 0.5–2 seconds on any visit after fonts are cached, 3–8 seconds on first visit (font load cost unavoidable).
The 451s → 2s improvement would be immediately and dramatically obvious.

*** initial - auto-resize case

Currently there is a bug with manually resizing columns.

For example when in auto resize mode and then trying to click with the mouse (and not relese yet) one of the column
resize handlers between two columns or the handler after the last column, the column width of all columns suddenly
changes and the mouse pointer is not even on the click position anymore. You still can drag the now not in focus slider
and the column itself (left from the original resize handler) resizes, but all other colums also resize, the columns
left and right from the currently resized columns shrink becasue it looks like as if there is hard limit for all column sizes together.

This is very obvious when clicking the last resize handler after the last column. All columns actually shrink when
dragging to the right (so when trying to increase the size of the last column)

The expected behaviour should be, when clicking and dragging a resize handler only the column to the left should
increase or shrink and all other column sizes should NOT be affected at all.

#+begin_example
Now I have a complete picture of the bug. Here's the analysis:

  ---
  Bug Analysis: Column Resize Disturbs All Columns

  Root cause — two interrelated issues in makeColumnsResizable → mousedown handler (lines 16219–16273)

  Issue 1: Layout switch at mousedown redistributes all widths

  Auto-resize (toggleAutoResizeColumns / toggleSubTableAutoResize) leaves the table in this state:

  ┌─────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐
  │        Property         │                Value                │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ table.style.tableLayout │ 'auto'                              │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ table.style.width       │ totalWidthPx (explicit fixed total) │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ visible <col> elements  │ no explicit width set               │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ <th> elements           │ minWidth = Xpx set                  │
  └─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┘

  The auto-resize deliberately skips setting col.style.width on visible columns (line 17174–17178 and 16694–16698) because it uses the auto layout with th.minWidth as the floor.

  When the user clicks a resize handle, mousedown (line 16262) immediately does:

  table.style.tableLayout = 'fixed';

  In table-layout: fixed with no explicit col.style.width on visible columns, the browser redistributes the fixed table.style.width equally among all columns. If the table was 1500px wide with 8 unequal
  columns, all of them jump to 187.5px at the moment of click — before the user has even moved the mouse. That is the "sudden change when clicking" the user describes.

  Issue 2: Zero-sum sizing during drag

  After the layout switch, table.style.width is still the fixed total set by auto-resize. Only the target column's <col> width is updated during drag. Because the table has a hard total width and the other
  columns still have no explicit widths, the browser distributes (table.width − targetCol.width) among them. Widening the target column compresses every other column proportionally. This is the "hard limit for
  all column sizes together" behavior.

  The last-column case is the clearest demonstration: with table-layout: fixed and a fixed table width, dragging the last column right cannot increase the total table width, so the browser must shrink other
  columns to compensate — which is why all columns shrink when dragging right on the last handle.

  ---
  What the fix needs to do (two changes, both in mousedown)

  1. Lock every column's current width before switching layout.
  Read th.offsetWidth for all columns (not just the dragged one) and write those values as explicit col.style.width on every <col> in the colgroup. This means the tableLayout: fixed switch sees a
  fully-specified colgroup and performs no redistribution — every column stays exactly where it was.

  2. Remove the fixed total-width constraint on the table.
  Set table.style.width = 'auto' (and clear table.style.minWidth) after locking individual column widths. With table-layout: fixed and all columns having explicit widths, the table's rendered width is the sum
  of its column widths. Removing the fixed total means widening one column expands the table instead of triggering a zero-sum compression of the others.

  These two changes leave onMouseMove and onMouseUp essentially unchanged — the drag only updates _targetCol.style.width, the table grows to accommodate, and all other columns are unaffected.

✻ Crunched for 2m 47s

※ recap: Analyzing a manual column resize bug where clicking a resize handle jumps all column widths. Next: implement the two-part fix in the mousedown handler inside makeColumnsResizable.

#+begin_example
Question 1: Does the bug fire without auto-resize?

  Yes, same two-cause structure.

  Without auto-resize active:
  - table.style.tableLayout is unset (browser default: auto)
  - table.style.width is unset (table sizes to content/container)
  - No <col> elements exist (no colgroup at all)

  On mousedown, lines 16252–16262:
  // Fresh colgroup created — all <col> elements have NO width
  let _cg = document.createElement('colgroup');
  for (let _ci = 0; _ci < _colCount; _ci++) {
      _cg.appendChild(document.createElement('col'));  // no width set
  }
  // Then immediately:
  table.style.tableLayout = 'fixed';

  With table-layout: fixed, no explicit col.style.width on any column, and no explicit table.style.width: the browser distributes the container's available width equally among all columns. All columns jump to
  containerWidth / columnCount at the moment of click — the same sudden redistribution as with auto-resize.

  The only difference from the auto-resize case is what the table is compared against. With auto-resize: totalWidthPx / colCount. Without: containerWidth / colCount. Either way, equal redistribution fires and
  kills the original layout.

  ---
  Question 2: Does the code honour a per-column minimum width?

  No. The only floor is the hardcoded literal on line 16287:

  _dragPendingWidth = Math.max(30, startWidth + (e.pageX - startX));

  30px is far too small to render any header content legibly. There is no code that:
  - Measures the natural width of the header content
  - Derives a per-column minimum from its widgets
  - Enforces that minimum during the drag

  What the minimum should actually be

  Each <th> has a .mb-col-hdr-flex div (a flex row) containing these children in order:

  ┌──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐
  │          Child           │     Always present?      │          Description           │
  ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Text node: colName       │ Yes                      │ Column name + space            │
  ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .sort-icon-btn × 3       │ Yes                      │ ⇅, ▲, ▼                        │
  ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .mb-col-uniq-wrap        │ Yes                      │ [count]📊 unique-values widget │
  ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .mb-col-collapse-hdr-btn │ Collapsable columns only │ ▶N▤ / ▼N▤                      │
  ├──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .mb-caa-col-hdr-btn      │ CAA/EAA columns only     │ ▶/▼ glyph + 16×16 <img>        │
  └──────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘

  The correct minimum is the natural (unwrapped) width of this flex container — i.e., the smallest width at which all children fit without being clipped or overflowing. The reliable way to measure this is
  th.querySelector('.mb-col-hdr-flex').scrollWidth before any drag-induced resizing changes the layout. scrollWidth returns the total scroll width of content even when the element is narrower than its content,
  so it gives exactly the "width needed to show everything" regardless of the current column width.

  This minimum must be measured once at mousedown time (before writing any widths), then used as the floor in onMouseMove instead of the hardcoded 30.
#+end_example

The code looks exactly right. Here's a summary of the three changes made, all within makeColumnsResizable:

  1. New variable _minWidth (line 16221)
  Initialised to 30 (safe fallback), updated at mousedown from the actual header flex content.

  2. mousedown handler — four new steps (lines 16252–16303)

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                        Step                         │            What            │                                                          Why                                                          │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Measure _hdrFlex.scrollWidth + 8                    │ Per-column header          │ scrollWidth = natural unwrapped width of colName + ⇅▲▼ + unique widget + optional collapse/CAA buttons; +8 for the    │
  │                                                     │ min-width                  │ 8px resizer handle                                                                                                    │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Read all th.offsetWidth before any mutation         │ Snapshot current visual    │ Values reflect whatever layout was active (auto or fixed) at click time                                               │
  │                                                     │ widths                     │                                                                                                                       │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Set col.style.width on every <col> + clear          │ Lock columns               │ Prevents table-layout:fixed from redistributing all widths equally; removing th.style.minWidth stops auto-resize's    │
  │ th.style.minWidth                                   │                            │ cell floors from interfering                                                                                          │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Clear table.style.width and table.style.minWidth    │ Free total-width           │ Table now sizes to exactly its column sum — widening one column grows the table instead of compressing the others     │
  │                                                     │ constraint                 │                                                                                                                       │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  3. onMouseMove floor (line 16327)
  Math.max(30, …) → Math.max(_minWidth, …) — drag stops at the header content boundary instead of the arbitrary 30px.

#+begin_example
Now I have the complete picture. Here is the analysis:

  ---
  Root cause

  The behavior is real and is caused entirely by normalizeCommentSpans setting white-space: nowrap permanently on live DOM elements in every call path — not just during measurement. It is unrelated to
  9.99.604–607, 9.99.614, and 9.99.625–626.

  ---
  What normalizeCommentSpans does to the live DOM

  After every render and filter/sort pass:

  Part A (added progressively in 9.99.639→9.99.647):
  - Sets commentSpan.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap' on every <span class="comment"> in every <td> (line 8267)
  - Sets bdi.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap' on the <bdi> inside every such span (line 8264)

  Part B (added in 9.99.651):
  - Sets td.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap' on every <td> whose direct child is a <span class="comment"> (line 8291) — covers the sticky Release column
  - Sets li.style.whiteSpace = 'nowrap' on every <li> whose direct child is a <span class="comment"> (line 8296) — covers the Label column's <li> elements

  This is what you see in the sample HTML: <li style="white-space: nowrap;"> and <span class="comment" style="white-space: nowrap;">.

  ---
  Why this creates a column minimum width in table-layout: auto

  In table-layout: auto (the default without auto-resize), the browser determines each column's width from the min-content width of its cells. Setting white-space: nowrap on a <li> or <span class="comment">
  containing a long disambiguation comment — e.g. "owned by Sony Music Entertainment, worldwide except JP; formerly owned by CBS between 1938–1990 within US/CA/MX" — forces that element's min-content width to
  the full single-line text width (potentially several hundred pixels). The browser then makes the entire column at least that wide.

  This is exactly the problem v9.99.642's changelog identified: "applying white-space: nowrap to span.comment in the live table changes those spans' min-content width to their full single-line text width,
  causing table-layout: auto to re-redistribute column widths". v9.99.642 attempted to fix this via pure DOM normalisation without any white-space mutation — but subsequent versions (9.99.647, 9.99.651)
  reintroduced white-space: nowrap on live cells to solve the anchor→comment break problem.

  The docstring justification (lines 8191–8195) — "Setting nowrap on the live container just makes the live cell match what was measured — no min-content change, no re-layout" — is only correct when
  auto-resize has already applied explicit column widths. Without auto-resize, table-layout: auto uses min-content widths dynamically, so setting white-space: nowrap on cells absolutely does change column
  widths.

  ---
  Which versions are responsible

  ┌───────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │   Version range   │                                                    Contribution                                                     │                          Responsible?                          │
  ├───────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9.99.604–607      │ Performance, hover highlight                                                                                        │ No                                                             │
  ├───────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9.99.614          │ Relationship column race condition                                                                                  │ No                                                             │
  ├───────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9.99.625–626      │ initCollapsableColumns perf — sets nowrap on <li> for measurement, then resets it to '' (line 33635)                │ No (temporary, cleaned up)                                     │
  ├───────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9.99.639–9.99.647 │ Progressive normalizeCommentSpans rewrites, ending with permanent white-space: nowrap on <span class="comment"> and │ Yes — Release column (sticky)                                  │
  │                   │  <bdi>                                                                                                              │                                                                │
  ├───────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9.99.651          │ Part B: permanent white-space: nowrap on <li> and <td>                                                              │ Yes — primary cause for the Label column and all <ul>-list     │
  │                   │                                                                                                                     │ columns                                                        │
  ├───────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9.99.652          │ Collapse-toggle size reservation                                                                                    │ No                                                             │
  └───────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  The minimum-width effect was present in partial form from 9.99.647 onward (disambiguation text in the Release/sticky column couldn't wrap), and became fully general in 9.99.651 when <li> elements were also
  locked

*** fix the nowrap on live DOM without breaking the anchor→comment wrap

What would that mean: "fix the nowrap on live DOM without breaking the anchor→comment wrap"

#+begin_example
 Now I have the full picture. Here is the conceptual analysis — no code changes.

  ---
  The tension being described

  What we want to prevent (the anchor→comment break):

  MusicBrainz renders releases and labels like:
  <a class="wrap-anywhere" href="…"><bdi>Title text</bdi></a>
  \n    ← whitespace text node, collapses to a space
  <span class="comment"><bdi>(disambiguation)</bdi></span>

  The browser has two independent break opportunities here:
  1. The collapsed-space text node between </a> and <span.comment> — lets the comment block drop to a new line
  2. The unicode-bidi: isolate bidi boundary inside <span.comment> — orphan ) outside <bdi> becomes a break point in bidi layout

  Both make disambiguation text appear orphaned on its own line, which looks wrong.

  What normalizeCommentSpans does to fix it:

  Sets white-space: nowrap on the live container (<li>, <td>, <span.comment>, <bdi>) to prevent all wrapping in the cell. That eliminates both break points, but it eliminates ALL break points — which is the
  over-broad part.

  The side effect:

  In table-layout: auto (default, no auto-resize), the browser determines each column's width from cell min-content widths. With white-space: nowrap on a <li> or <td>, the min-content of that cell becomes the
  full single-line text width of the longest no-wrap content. "Label (owned by Sony Music Entertainment, worldwide except JP; formerly owned by CBS between 1938–1990 within US/CA/MX)" is now an indivisible
  500+ px unit → the Label column must be at least that wide → users see what they're reporting.

  ---
  Why DOM manipulation alone (no white-space) keeps failing

  The 9.99.639→9.99.651 history shows six attempts at pure DOM fixes. The core reason they kept failing is this: <a class="wrap-anywhere"> has MusicBrainz's overflow-wrap: anywhere applied via its stylesheet.
  That CSS property allows a break at any Unicode code point — not just at spaces, but including at the boundary between the anchor element and its next sibling. Simply removing the whitespace text node
  between </a> and <span.comment> is not enough, because overflow-wrap: anywhere on the anchor will still break at the element boundary even with no space character there.

  ---
  The three conceptual approaches for a true fix

  Approach A — display: inline-block wrapper + overflow-wrap: normal !important inside

  Wrap <a>+<span.comment> in a <span style="display:inline-block; overflow-wrap:normal !important">. Inside:
  - overflow-wrap: normal !important overrides the anchor's anywhere (inline !important wins the cascade over any stylesheet rule)
  - With overflow-wrap: normal, breaks only occur at space characters
  - Remove the whitespace text node between </a> and <span.comment> (already done by normalizeCommentSpans) → no break between them
  - Normalise <span.comment> interior (already done) → no bdi-boundary break

  Min-content of the wrapper becomes the longest individual word in the title + comment text (not the full line). "Entertainment," might be 90px; "Shuffle" 55px — negligible compared to the current 500px
  forced minimum.

  The complication: ERG injects a ▶ button via a.parentNode.insertBefore(btn, a). If <a> is inside the wrapper, a.parentNode is the wrapper span, so ERG's ▶ ends up inside it. Visually that's fine, but
  idempotency under repeated normalizeCommentSpans calls (filter/sort re-renders) needs careful guarding — specifically, the function must recognise an already-wrapped pair and skip it, even with an ERG ▶
  prepended inside.

  Approach B — Word Joiner (U+2060) character

  Replace the whitespace text node between </a> and <span.comment> with a U+2060 Word Joiner text node (zero-width, invisible, explicitly prevents a line break at its position). Continue interior
  normalisation. Set no white-space style anywhere.

  The problem: the CSS Line Breaking Algorithm spec says overflow-wrap: anywhere generates break opportunities even at Word Joiners — it overrides the no-break hint. So U+2060 would not reliably prevent the
  break when the anchor has overflow-wrap: anywhere. This approach is unreliable in the face of MusicBrainz's stylesheet.

  Approach C — Conditional nowrap: only apply in auto-resize mode

  The docstring says "Setting nowrap on the live container just makes the live cell match what was measured — no min-content change". That reasoning is only valid when columns already have explicit fixed
  widths (i.e., auto-resize has locked them in). Move the white-space: nowrap mutations so they only run when isAutoResized is true — not at the three non-auto-resize call sites (main render, filter/sort,
  load-from-disk). In default column mode, retain the interior DOM normalisation (bdi-boundary and whitespace-node removal) and accept that on very narrow columns the anchor→comment break might occasionally
  appear.

  This is the lowest-risk change and correctly models the original intent: the nowrap mutations are about making live cells match already-measured widths, which only means something when auto-resize has
  measured them.

  ---
  Summary of the trade-offs

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                     Approach                     │  Eliminates the min-content   │                    Eliminates anchor→comment break?                     │             Risk / complexity              │
  │                                                  │           problem?            │                                                                         │                                            │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ A — inline-block wrapper + overflow-wrap:normal  │ Yes (min-content = longest    │ Yes                                                                     │ ERG interaction requires careful           │
  │ !important                                       │ word)                         │                                                                         │ idempotency guarding                       │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ B — Word Joiner                                  │ Yes (no style mutation)       │ Unreliable — overflow-wrap:anywhere overrides U+2060                    │ Simple change, but doesn't reliably work   │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ C — nowrap only in auto-resize mode              │ Yes (default mode unaffected) │ Partial — interior normalization still runs, but overflow-wrap:anywhere │ Low risk, pragmatic trade-off              │
  │                                                  │                               │  can still break                                                        │                                            │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Approach A is the most principled solution; Approach C is the safest incremental fix that restores original default behaviour while keeping the auto-resize mode working exactly as designed.
#+end_example

#+begin_example
Now I have everything I need. Here are the three answers:

  ---
  Q1: Allow drag-narrower with line-breaking in auto-resize mode

  Not possible with the current normalizeCommentSpans approach. After auto-resize runs, every <li>, <td>, <span.comment> and <bdi> that contains disambiguation text has white-space: nowrap written as an inline
  style on the live element. Our makeColumnsResizable fix (from earlier in this session) correctly updates col.style.width to the dragged narrower width and switches to table-layout: fixed, so the column
  genuinely becomes narrower — but the cells themselves still carry white-space: nowrap, so the text cannot wrap regardless of how narrow the column is. It overflows or clips instead of breaking. Answering Q1
  requires that no live cell element carries white-space: nowrap.

  ---
  Q2: Restore button should return to native MusicBrainz layout

  restoreOriginalTableState (line 16800) restores:
  - th.style.minWidth = ''
  - table.style.width, table.style.minWidth, table.style.tableLayout
  - The colgroup

  It does not touch any cell-level inline styles. But there is a second problem that makes this worse: normalizeCommentSpans is called at render time (lines 24907, 28213, 30621) — before
  storeOriginalTableState is ever invoked (which only happens at the first user drag). So the snapshot of "original state" was already taken after normalizeCommentSpans had written white-space: nowrap onto
  every cell. Restoring to that snapshot brings back the nowrap cells. The "original" that gets stored is not the native MusicBrainz DOM state — it is a post-normalisation state that already has all the nowrap
  inline styles present.

  ---
  Q3: Does Approach C answer Q1 and Q2?

  No to Q1, and only partially to Q2.

  Tracing the four relevant scenarios under Approach C (nowrap mutations only when isAutoResized === true):

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┬────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                Scenario                 │ Q1 /   │                                                               Works under Approach C?                                                                │
  │                                         │   Q2   │                                                                                                                                                      │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Never used auto-resize — default mode   │ Q2     │ ✓ — isAutoResized is false at all render call sites, so nowrap mutations never fire, storeOriginalTableState snapshots clean cells, restore returns  │
  │                                         │        │ to native layout                                                                                                                                     │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Never used auto-resize — user drags     │ Q1     │ ✓ — cells have no nowrap, text breaks naturally                                                                                                      │
  │ narrower                                │        │                                                                                                                                                      │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Auto-resize active — user drags         │ Q1     │ ✗ — normalizeCommentSpans was called with isAutoResized = true inside toggleAutoResizeColumns, nowrap styles are on cells, dragging narrower clips   │
  │ narrower                                │        │ instead of wrapping                                                                                                                                  │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────┼────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Auto-resize active — user clicks        │ Q2     │ ✗ — nowrap was applied when auto-resize ran; restoreOriginalTableState does not clear cell-level inline styles; cells keep white-space: nowrap after │
  │ Restore                                 │        │  restore                                                                                                                                             │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────┴────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  What would fully answer both Q1 and Q2:

  Remove the white-space: nowrap style mutations from normalizeCommentSpans entirely — never write them to live DOM elements under any mode. The measurement sandbox already uses white-space: nowrap !important
  via .mb-measure-nowrap, so auto-resize measurements are unaffected. The DOM interior normalisation (bdi-boundary consolidation and whitespace-node removal between </a> and <span.comment>) would remain, which
  is enough to eliminate the most common break points without affecting cell min-content widths in table-layout: auto.

  The residual risk is that overflow-wrap: anywhere on <a class="wrap-anywhere"> can still permit a break between the anchor and the comment even with no whitespace text node between them. In practice this
  would only occur if the column is narrower than the auto-resize minimum, which is exactly the case where you want wrapping anyway. At the auto-resize minimum width the full content fits on one line and the
  browser won't insert unnecessary breaks.

✻ Sautéed for 2m 40s

※ recap: Fixing column resize bugs in a MusicBrainz userscript. The next step is removing white-space nowrap mutations from live DOM cells in normalizeCommentSpans entirely, keeping only the interior DOM
  normalization.
#+end_example

#+begin_example
Done. Here's what was changed for v9.99.669:

  Root cause: The v9.99.668 live-table measurement uses th.offsetWidth, but any table with style.display = 'none' (initially-collapsed sub-tables from renderGroupedTable's shouldStayOpen logic) returns
  offsetWidth = 0. This produced a 20px minWidth on every column of every collapsed sub-table, making them look broken when expanded.

  Fix (lines 17123–17148): Before adding mb-measure-nowrap, detect _tableWasHidden = table.style.display === 'none' and briefly set display = ''. After removing mb-measure-nowrap, restore display = 'none'.
  Both DOM mutations are synchronous with no await between them — the browser never paints the intermediate state. This runs on every toggleAutoResizeColumns() call, so both the initial auto-trigger and
  subsequent manual Resize clicks now correctly size all sub-tables regardless of their collapsed/expanded state.
#+end_example

** Are the changes in commit "998e768" still necessary
*** initial

Are the changes for v9.99.652 in commit "998e768" still necessary, after all the resize fixes ?

#+begin_example
Yes, the PASS 2 collapse-toggle compensation is still necessary, and here is why.

  ---
  Why PASS 2 is still needed

  .mb-cell-collapse-toggle is position: absolute; right: 4px — it is out of flow. Out-of-flow elements never contribute to a cell's layout width, regardless of the measurement approach:

  - th.offsetWidth (live-table nowrap, v9.99.668): reads the max border-box width across all cells in the column, but position:absolute descendants are excluded from that box entirely.
  - offscreen measureDiv (old approach, still used by toggleSubTableAutoResize): same exclusion — absolutely-positioned elements don't push the div wider.

  Without PASS 2, auto-resize sizes each column to exactly its in-flow content minimum, and the toggle widget visually overlaps the rightmost characters of long cells.

  ---
  One subtle formula shift in toggleAutoResizeColumns

  The PASS 2 formula is:

  extra = max(0, toggleWidth + 16 − thPaddingRight)

  In the old offscreen approach (pre-v9.99.668), columnWidths[colIndex] was built from the offscreen div using TH padding, so thPaddingRight correctly represented the right padding already baked into the
  measurement.

  In the new live-table approach (v9.99.668+), columnWidths[colIndex] = th.offsetWidth already reflects the real TD padding in the column. The toggle sits at right: 4px from the TD's padding box edge, so
  strictly speaking the baseline should now be tdPaddingRight (≈22px) rather than thPaddingRight (≈5px).

  Effect: because tdPaddingRight > thPaddingRight, the formula currently over-estimates extra by roughly (tdPaddingRight − thPaddingRight) ≈ 17px. That means columns with a collapse toggle are slightly wider
  than the absolute minimum — a conservative over-allocation that causes no visual harm.

  ---
  toggleSubTableAutoResize — unchanged

  This function still uses the old offscreen measureDiv approach (it was never migrated to the live-table approach). Its PASS 2 is identical to the original and still correct for the offscreen context.

  ---
  Conclusion: v9.99.652 changes remain necessary. The only thing worth noting is that PASS 2's formula in toggleAutoResizeColumns now slightly over-estimates extra by ~17px per toggle column — which is a
  harmless cosmetic widening, not a correctness problem.

    /**
     * Prepares the table header row for the final rendered view.
     *
     * Three sequential passes are performed:
     *
     *   1. **Column removal** — removes columns whose header text prefix matches
     *      an entry in `removalMap` and whose corresponding setting is enabled
     *      (e.g. sa_remove_rel, sa_remove_rating, sa_remove_tagger, …).
     *
     *   2. **Column origin stamping** — stamps each surviving original <th> with
     *      the CSS class `mb-original-column`.  Idempotent: already-stamped cells
     *      from a re-render pass are skipped.
     *
     *   3. **Synthetic column injection** — injects new <th> elements for each
     *      configured extractor, assigning:
     *        - `mb-extracted-column`         for activeColumnExtractors entries
     *                                        and extractMainColumn (MB-Name/Comment)
     *        - `mb-derived-extracted-column` for activeSyntheticColumnExtractors
     *                                        entries (second-pass derivations)
     *      Each injected <th> also receives `dataset.colName`, the appropriate
     *      background color from settings, and is appended to the header row if
     *      not already present (idempotent across re-renders).
     *
     * The three CSS classes are the authoritative source for the Statistics panel
     * column-origin breakdown (original / extracted / derived counts).
     *
     * @param {HTMLTableSectionElement|HTMLTableRowElement} headerElement
     *   The `<thead>` element or its first `<tr>` row to process.
     */

    /**
     * Returns a human-readable tooltip describing a synthetic column header.
     *
     * The tooltip is stamped onto the <th> element injected by cleanupHeaders()
     * so users can hover over any synthetic column name and instantly see which
     * source column it was extracted from and what the column contains.

     * @param {string} extractor     - The extractor key (e.g. 'splitCountryDate').

     * @param {string} colName       - The synthetic column name (e.g. 'Country').
     * @returns {string} Tooltip text, or '' when no description is available.
     */

    /**
     * Probes the Resource Timing API for the most recent PerformanceResourceEntry
     * that matches `url` and classifies it as a memory-cache hit, disk-cache hit,
     * network fetch, or "timing unavailable" (no entry / API absent).
     *
     * Classification rules (in priority order):
     *
     *   1. transferSize === 0 AND encodedBodySize > 0
     *        → Memory cache (🟢).  Browser served from RAM; size is known even
     *          for cross-origin resources when served from memory.
     *
     *   2. transferSize > 0
     *        → Network fetch (🔵).  Actual bytes received over the wire.
     *
     *   3. transferSize === 0 AND encodedBodySize === 0 AND duration < 5 ms
     *        → Disk cache (🟡).  Both size fields are 0 (opaque cross-origin) but
     *          the response arrived in under 5 ms — consistent with a disk-cached
     *          redirect chain where BOTH the redirect and the final resource are
     *          served from cache.
     *          NOTE: this path is NEVER triggered for coverartarchive.org /
     *          eventartarchive.org.  Their CDN issues non-cacheable 302 redirects
     *          (Cache-Control: no-store or max-age=0), so the redirect round-trip
     *          always adds 2–4 s of network latency and duration never drops below
     *          5 ms on a page reload.  🟡 is therefore only observable for image
     *          URLs that are served directly (no redirect) or whose redirect chain
     *          is genuinely disk-cached.
     *
     *   4. transferSize === 0 AND encodedBodySize === 0 AND duration >= 5 ms
     *        → Network / redirect chain (🔵).  This is the only outcome ever
     *          produced for CAA/EAA archive URLs on any repeated page load, because
     *          the non-cacheable redirect to archive.org always requires a fresh
     *          network round-trip.  Even if the final image bytes are already in
     *          the disk cache, the redirect latency keeps duration > 5 ms.
     *
     *   5. No matching entry, or Performance API absent
     *        → Timing unavailable (⚠️).  This is the ONLY case that returns
     *          'unavailable'; every case where an entry exists resolves to one of
     *          the three statuses above.
     *
     * Returned object shape:
     * ```
     * {
     *   status:          'memory' | 'disk' | 'network' | 'unavailable',
     *   transferSize:    number | null,
     *   encodedBodySize: number | null,
     *   duration:        number | null,
     *   redirectStart:   number | null,   // 0 for opaque cross-origin
     *   responseStart:   number | null,   // 0 for opaque cross-origin
     * }
     * ```
     *
     * @param  {string} url  The exact URL to look up (matched against entry.name).
     * @returns {{ status: string, transferSize: number|null, encodedBodySize: number|null,
     *             duration: number|null, redirectStart: number|null, responseStart: number|null }}
     */
    /**
     * Determines the correct cache-hint status and label for a loaded image
     * source URL, taking the IDB/memory/native-path distinction into account.
     *
     * The core problem this solves: when IDB is enabled and an image is fetched
     * via GM_xmlhttpRequest (_artGmFetchBlob), the result is stored as a blob:
     * URL.  Blob: URLs are never recorded by the browser's Resource Timing API,
     * so getResourceTimingHint(blobUrl) always returns 'unavailable' → ⚠️.
     * The correct status in this case is 'network' (the GM_xhr fetch IS a
     * genuine network request).
     *
     * When IDB is disabled the browser fetches images directly via <img>.src
     * (a real https:// URL), which IS recorded by the RT API.
     *
     * Decision logic:
     *   • fromIdb    → synthesise 'idb'
     *   • fromMemory → synthesise 'memory'
     *   • src starts with 'blob:' → synthesise 'network'  (GM_xhr IDB path)
     *   • otherwise → query getResourceTimingHint(src)     (native img.src path)
     *
     * @param {string}  src         Resolved image URL (blob: or https://).
     * @param {boolean} fromIdb     Whether the blob was served from IDB.
     * @param {boolean} fromMemory  Whether the blob was served from session Map.
     * @returns {{ status: string, label: string }}
     */
#+end_example

     *          network round-trip.  Even if the final image bytes are already in
     *          the disk cache, the redirect latency keeps duration > 5 ms.
     *
     *   5. No matching entry, or Performance API absent
     *        → Timing unavailable (⚠️).  This is the ONLY case that returns
     *          'unavailable'; every case where an entry exists resolves to one of
     *          the three statuses above.
     *
     * Returned object shape:
     * ```
     * {
     *   status:          'memory' | 'disk' | 'network' | 'unavailable',
     *   transferSize:    number | null,
     *   encodedBodySize: number | null,
     *   duration:        number | null,
     *   redirectStart:   number | null,   // 0 for opaque cross-origin
     *   responseStart:   number | null,   // 0 for opaque cross-origin
     * }
     * ```
     *
     * @param  {string} url  The exact URL to look up (matched against entry.name).
     * @returns {{ status: string, transferSize: number|null, encodedBodySize: number|null,
     *             duration: number|null, redirectStart: number|null, responseStart: number|null }}
     */
#+end_example

#+begin_example
    /**
     * Wires the single global ▶/◀ toggle button for multi-table mode.
     *
     * In multi-table mode `initCollapsableColumns` is called once per sub-table
     * (because each rendered `<table>` is independent), so it cannot accumulate
     * all column-header buttons into one `collapseHdrBtns` array.  This helper
     * fills that role: it is called once after ALL sub-tables have been
     * processed by `initCollapsableColumns`, scans the live DOM for every
     * `.mb-col-collapse-hdr-btn` across every `table.tbl`, and then:
     *
     *   • Hides the global button when no such buttons exist (none of the
     *     filtered-in sub-tables has a multi-row column).
     *   • Shows the global button and re-wires its `onclick` to drive every
     *     found header button (and therefore every cell toggle across every
     *     sub-table) to the target expanded/collapsed state.
     *   • Calls `updateGlobalCollapseButtonHighlight(null)` to apply or clear
     *     the highlight tint on the global button based on the current filter
     *     match state across all sub-tables.
     *
     * Must be called from `renderGroupedTable` after the `dataArray.forEach`
     * loop completes — both on initial render and on every filter re-run.
     */
    /**
     * _applyCollapseState — expand or collapse a single multi-row cell toggle
     * WITHOUT dispatching a synthetic click event.
     *
     * Calling `toggle.click()` from within another click handler is suppressed
     * by some browsers / userscript managers because the dispatched MouseEvent
     * has `isTrusted = false`.  This helper replicates the delegation-handler
     * logic from `ensureCollapseDelegate` directly so that mass-expand /
     * mass-collapse from column-header, sub-table, and global collapse buttons
     * works in all environments.
     *
     * @param {HTMLSpanElement} toggle  - The `.mb-cell-collapse-toggle` span.
     * @param {boolean}         expand  - true → expand; false → collapse.
     */
#+end_example

    /**
     * Populates the shared bigbox tooltip `tip` (already cleared by the caller)
     * according to the active page definition's `tooltipColumns` and
     * `extractMainColumn` features.
     *
     * tooltipColumns element forms:
     *   \'---'             → horizontal divider rule
     *   plain string      → one text row from the matching column.
     *                        When the column name equals `extractMainColumn`,
     *                        the title is rendered bold and any disambiguation
     *                        comment (from `<span class="comment">`) appears in
     *                        italic below it.
     *   JS array of tokens → single inline row.  Each token is either a column
     *                        name (resolved to cell text) or a literal punctuation
     *                        string \'(\', \')\', \'-\', etc. (rendered as-is).
     *                        The whole line is omitted when every column token
     *                        resolves to an empty string.  Adjacent literals are
     *                        suppressed when their neighbouring column value is
     *                        absent.
     *
     * @param {HTMLDivElement}      tip      Cleared tooltip div to populate.
     * @param {HTMLTableRowElement} row      The hovered data row.
     * @param {object|null}         pageDef  Active page definition (may be null).
     * @param {HTMLTableElement}    table    Owning table (for header lookups).
     * @returns {boolean}  true when tooltipColumns was applied;
     *                     false when the feature is absent (caller must fall back).
     */

    /**
     * Renders the artist-roles list from an Artists column cell into the tooltip.
     *
     * MusicBrainz event "Artists" cells contain a `.artist-roles-container` div
     * with a `<ul class="artist-roles">` whose `<li>` items follow this pattern:
     *
     *   <li>
     *     <span class="name-variation"><a href="…"><bdi>Artist Name</bdi></a></span>
     *     (role text)
     *   </li>
     *
     * or (without name-variation span):
     *
     *   <li>
     *     <a href="…"><bdi>Artist Name</bdi></a> (role text)
     *   </li>
     *
     * ALL <li> elements are read regardless of their inline `display:none` style
     * (MusicBrainz collapses extras behind the ▶ toggle; we want the full list).
     *
     * Each entry is rendered as "Name (role)", entries comma-separated on one line.
     *
     * @param {HTMLTableRowElement} row  Data row.
     * @param {number}              ci   Column index of the Artists cell.
     * @param {HTMLDivElement}      tip  Tooltip div to append the artists line to.
     * @returns {boolean}  true when at least one artist entry was appended.
     */
#+end_example

** findings
*** FYI — non-doc issues noticed (not part of this task, flagging only)

  - synItemCount's panel-height heuristic is missing several *ValueCounts families in its sum (same staleness pattern its neighbor panelBadgeChWidth already got fixed for) — likely harmless since the result is
    clamped, but a candidate for a future look.
  - caaYesCount/caaNoCount (46328–46329) are self-documented dead locals ("unused after 9.99.569") — this was actually already caught and removed on the separate dead-code-audit branch, which hasn't been
    merged here yet, so it's still present on jsdoc-audit.

*** FYI - REL_DISCOGRAPHY_MAPPINGS is populated but never read — dead code, already caught and removed on the separate (unmerged) dead-code-audit branch. Not acting on it here.

*** FYI — real bugs noticed (not strictly JSDoc, but user-visible)

- Stale hardcoded shortcut list: the debug/console log fired every time prefix mode is entered (two call sites, lines ~15245/15255) lists 13 shortcut keys but is missing 3 real ones now in ctrlMFunctionMap:
  b (Barcode Highlighting), g (Focus Global Filter), c (Focus Next Column Filter). showShortcutsHelp()'s own displayed list is complete and correct — only this debug string drifted.
- openSettingsWithConfigButtons() has the same already-fixed-elsewhere dead-local-variable pattern (_fnRegistry) as chunk-1's _fnRegistry finding — already caught on the separate unmerged dead-code-audit
  branch, not acting on it here.

*** DONE FYI — 2 real bugs found (not JSDoc, but worth fixing alongside)

 1. determineMaxPageFromDOM (line ~37571) — the same unreachable-Lib.debug()-after-return bug I already fixed once in chunk 1 (on a different function). This is a separate, un-fixed instance in this function.
 2. Third debug/user-edits-wrong.org reference (line ~38404, inside startFetchingProcess) — same stale-file fix as the two already done in 7a/7c

        // :is(#content,#page) covers both the standard div#content wrapper and the

        const SELECTOR =
            ':is(#content,#page) table.tbl > tbody > tr > td a[href^="/release"],' +
            ':is(#content,#page) table.tbl > tbody > tr > td a[href*="musicbrainz.org/release"]';
        const links    = document.querySelectorAll(SELECTOR);

#+begin_example
Context

 ShowAllEntityData.user.js already has a "unique column value" dropdown (opened via
 the 📊 icon in a column header, see openUniqDrop()) that lists every distinct value
 present in a column with an occurrence count, and a quickfilter search box. Today,
 clicking a value replaces the column's text filter with that single value and
 closes the dropdown — only one value can be filtered on at a time per column.

 The user wants this dropdown to support checkboxes, so multiple values can be
 selected at once (OR'd together within the column), matching a pattern already used
 in a sibling project (springsteen-site-parser's smarttable.js, used by
 BruceBaseParser.user.js). That reference implementation's semantics — which this
 plan ports (not its code, since the architectures differ) — are:

 - Checked values within one column are OR'd (row passes if its value is checked).
 - An empty checked-set means no constraint (show all rows for that column), not
 "match nothing."
 - Selecting a checkbox in one column still ANDs against other active column
 filters (unchanged, pre-existing behavior).
 - Checkbox mode is mutually exclusive with plain-text filtering on the same column:
 typing text cancels a checkbox selection, and vice versa (mirrors how the existing
 mbMultirowMode "Cell structure" filters already behave).

 The user confirmed (via clarifying questions) to keep this minimal:
 - No bulk-select-all-visible-on-Enter bonus feature.
 - No new in-panel "N selected / clear" UI — the existing per-column ✕ button
 already fully clears everything once the plan's cleanup edits land.
 - Column input summary label when 2+ values are checked: simply "N selected".

 All work happens on a new feature branch. Per this repo's CLAUDE.md, version bumps
 and ShowAllEntityData_CHANGELOG.json entries are main-only; this branch tracks
 changes in ShowAllEntityData_CHANGELOG.wip.json with placeholder WIP.N versions.
#+end_example

* DONE performance

#+begin_example
1 — .mb-measure-nowrap CSS rule (stylesheet injection)
Added a single <style> rule covering .mb-measure-nowrap and .mb-measure-nowrap * with white-space:nowrap !important, overflow-wrap:normal !important, word-break:normal !important. This is the enabler for fix 3.
2 — makeColumnsResizable: rAF-throttled onMouseMove + cached _targetCol

At mousedown, the colgroup is guaranteed to exist and the specific <col> element for the column being dragged is cached in _targetCol. The tableLayout:'fixed' switch also happens once here instead of on every write.
onMouseMove now only stores the desired width in _dragPendingWidth and sets a _dragRafPending flag. The actual col.style.width write happens inside a single requestAnimationFrame callback, capped to once per frame regardless of mouse event rate. The fast path writes directly to _targetCol and falls back to setColumnWidth() only if the element was detached by a concurrent re-render.
onMouseUp clears _targetCol and _dragRafPending.

3 — Global and subtable measurement loops: hoisted getComputedStyle + CSS class

A colStyleCache array is built once before any loop begins by calling getComputedStyle once per column header. The inner row loop reads from this cache — zero getComputedStyle calls per cell, down from one per cell (O(rows×cols) → O(cols)).
measureDiv.classList.add('mb-measure-nowrap') replaces the measureDiv.style.setProperty(…) calls on the div itself.
All measureDiv.querySelectorAll('*').forEach(el => el.style.setProperty(…)) loops — which fired once per cloned element per cell, including inside every <li> and every CAA/EAA art-li — are removed entirely. The CSS rule inherited by all children does the same job with zero JS and zero reflows.

4 — Sidebar MutationObserver: scoped to sidebar, rAF deduplicated

observer.observe(document.body, { childList:true, subtree:true }) → observer.observe(sidebar, { childList:true, subtree:true, attributes:true, attributeFilter:['class','style'] }). The observer now only fires when the sidebar itself changes, not on every DOM mutation anywhere on the page.
The requestAnimationFrame(() => updateHandlePosition(handle)) call inside the callback is guarded by _sidebarRafPending so bursts of sidebar mutations only queue one getBoundingClientRect() read per frame.

5 — window.scroll listener: rAF throttled

The unthrottled () => updateHandlePosition(handle) scroll handler is wrapped in the same rAF pending-flag pattern (_scrollRafPending), capping getBoundingClientRect() reads to one per paint cycle during scroll.
#+end_example

#+begin_example
Summary of fixes, prioritised
#IssueWhereImpactFix1mousemove writes col.style.width synchronously at mouse-event rateonMouseMove🔴 Freeze during dragWrap in requestAnimationFrame with pending-flag2getComputedStyle(cell) called per cell in nested loopsmeasurement loops (both)🔴 Freeze during auto-resizeHoist per-column style reads outside the row loop3querySelectorAll('*').forEach(setProperty) on every cell clonemeasurement loops🟡 Slow auto-resizeReplace with a CSS class + stylesheet rule4colgroup.querySelectorAll('col') re-queried every mousemove framesetColumnWidth🟡 Avoidable overhead during dragCache targetCol reference at mousedown5Body-level MutationObserver amplifies all DOM writes during resizesidebar observer🔴 Multiplies all aboveAlready identified — scope observer to sidebar element
#+end_example

  - /report/<Name>?filter=0|1 → report-detail page type, column-agnostic (native table.tbl already matches the expected DOM shape, pagination already handled by the existing generic fetchMaxPageGeneric). Two
  buttons toggle filter=0/filter=1 via the same params-override idiom used by user-tags.

  Supporting fixes:
  - Replaced the stale, never-committed @match .../report header line with correct /reports* and /report/* matches.
  - Special-cased pageType === 'reports-index' in both the live fetch-loop colName logic and its disk-load mirror, so the rendered column header is always the literal "Report" rather than a
  derived/singularized category name (a subtlety the initial design missed — caught by the Plan agent tracing _table.dataset.mbOriginalColName and finding it's dead code).
  - Added debug snapshots (debug/*.html) and debug/NOTES.md documentation per project convention.
  - Version bump + changelog entry.

  h2+ul walk produces exactly 117 rows across 14 sections as expected.

  /report/ArtistsThatMayBeGroups?filter=0, and /report/DuplicateArtists?filter=0) to confirm rendering, the filter buttons produce different row counts, and the DuplicateArtists checkbox column doesn't break

Is it possible to implement adding multiple columns to the "addCAA" parameter for the pageType "type: 'report-detail'", e.g.

#+begin_example
            features: {
	        ...
                addCAA: [ 'Release', 'Release group' ]
            },

#+begin_example
● Yes, this is quite feasible and low-risk. All the addCAA/addEAA consumers funnel column-name resolution through one helper, caaFindColumnByName(table, name) at ShowAllEntityData.user.js:41698, and everywhere
  else just does a truthiness check or passes the value straight through — so making that helper accept name: string | string[] (try each candidate against the table's headers, first match wins) would enable
  addCAA: ['Release', 'Release group'] with essentially one function changed, no changes needed at the ~4 call sites that read activeDefinition.features.addCAA.

  The one nuance: since report-detail covers 117 different column-agnostic reports, a given report's table will only ever have one of the candidate columns present (not both) — so semantics should be "first
  candidate found in this table wins," not "combine both," which is exactly what a simple ordered-candidate loop gives you.

  Want me to go ahead and implement it (update caaFindColumnByName, tweak debug/tooltip logging to display multi-candidate names nicely, and switch report-detail's addCAA to the array form)?
#+end_example

** Fix: CSP style-src silently blocking 9 inline <style> injections (incl. account-applications page)

     Context

     The user reported the account-applications page type (/account/applications) as
     "broken since a recent MusicBrainz server update." Investigation of
     debug/applications.html (old, working) vs debug/applications-new.html /
     debug/applications-new-final.html (new, broken) showed MusicBrainz added a new
     native "Digest access authentication" section (h2 + paragraphs + a functional
     <form> with two hidden CSRF inputs and Disable/Reset buttons). Tracing the
     render pipeline (parseDocumentForTables, renderGroupedTable,
     makeH2sCollapsible) showed the table-consolidation logic itself handles this
     fine — no crash, no data loss, no corruption.

     The user then supplied a screenshot of the live rendered page showing a raw,
     unstyled dump of "Unicode character map" picker rows (e.g. "Left Single Quote",
     "✕ Close (Esc)") appended below MusicBrainz's own site footer. This traced to
     initSaUnicodeCharsFeature()'s <style id="sa-unicode-menu-style"> block
     (ShowAllEntityData.user.js:42941-43038), whose #sa-unicode-menu { display: none; position: absolute; ... } rule normally keeps this Ctrl+U-triggered
     picker hidden. The user confirmed via a live browser console error that
     MusicBrainz's CSP header now reads:

     style-src 'self' staticbrainz.org static.metabrainz.org

     — no 'unsafe-inline', nonce, or hash — so the browser silently drops this
     (and any other) inline <style> element the script injects via
     document.createElement('style') + document.head.appendChild(...).

     Scope correction (verified via curl -I): this CSP is not site-wide.
     General content pages (/artist/..., /release-group/..., /search?...)
     are served by an edge layer (server: openresty) and return no
     content-security-policy header at all. /account/applications is served
     directly by the backend app (server: Plack::Handler::Starlet) and does
     carry the restrictive CSP. So today, the 9-site vulnerable pattern is only
     actually breaking rendering on /account/applications (and plausibly other
     account/* routes served the same way — unconfirmed). It is not currently
     degrading sticky headers, dialogs, etc. on general content pages.

     That said, all 9 sites use the identical CSP-fragile pattern, and a second,
     independent visual bug on this same page confirms the fix must still cover
     more than just the Unicode picker: the sub-table filter row's Cc/Rx/Ex
     checkboxes render stacked one-per-line instead of inline (user-supplied
     screenshot). Traced to .mb-subtable-filter-container /
     .mb-subtable-filter-container.visible (ShowAllEntityData.user.js:21460- 21470), which lives inside site #5 (the large main-toolbar <style>
     block) and sets display: inline-flex on .visible. With that stylesheet
     dropped by CSP, the container falls back to a plain <span>'s default
     display: inline, which doesn't establish a flex row; each <label> inside
     it independently carries an inline display: flex (via JS property
     assignment, so CSP-exempt) which computes to a block-level box, forcing each
     onto its own line. This is mechanistically the same root cause as the
     Unicode-picker bug, just via a different rule in the same blocked
     stylesheet — confirming site #5 needs the same fix, not just site #9.

     Given both confirmed symptoms live on /account/applications, and MusicBrainz
     could extend this CSP to more routes later, the user chose to convert all 9
     sites to GM_addStyle now rather than just the two currently-proven-broken
     ones (#5, #9) — it's a uniformly cheap, strictly-correct change either way.

     Two other observations from the account-applications investigation were
     ruled out as bugs and are intentionally out of scope: (1) the "Authorized
     applications" intro paragraph now renders after the table instead of before
     it — a mechanical, pre-existing side effect of how renderGroupedTable inserts
     new h3/table pairs immediately after the section header, which would equally
     affect the old page structure; (2) the new "Digest access authentication"
     section starts collapsed via makeH2sCollapsible() — this is the same
     generic behavior "Developer applications" already had, not a regression.

     Fix approach

     Add // @grant GM_addStyle to the userscript header and convert all 9
     document.createElement('style') + document.head.appendChild(...) sites to
     GM_addStyle(cssText). GM_addStyle runs in the userscript's privileged
     Tampermonkey context and is exempt from the page's CSP style-src
     restriction — unlike a plain DOM-inserted <style> element, which the CSP
     correctly treats as page content and blocks. GM_addStyle returns the
     created <style> HTMLElement (Tampermonkey semantics — the only GM engine
     this script targets, confirmed via existing GM_xmlhttpRequest/
     GM_registerMenuCommand usage), so any site that previously set .id on the
     element for a getElementById idempotency guard can keep doing so on the
     returned element. GM_addStyle takes a plain string, so the existing
     template-literal CSS with interpolated settings-driven colors (sites #1, #2)
     works unchanged.
