** write the four adapter files

write the four adapter files

#+begin_example
Four adapters committed (0bb4ce6). Here's what each one does and the non-obvious choices:

  jungleland.js — selects by a[target="inferioredx1"] (the only reliable selector on this class-free 1990s page), extracts date with /(YYYY-MM-DD)\s*$/ from link text, and version from _N.htm filename suffix.

  brucespringsteen-it.js — one file handles both official and unofficial via a get columnDefs() getter that reads the URL at render time. Walks a[href^="detrec.aspx"] → closest('b'), iterates child nodes
  manually to get text before the first <br> (handles the yellow PROMO span being mid-line). Notes live in <i><u> outside the <b> but inside the same <p>.

  archive-org.js — the search page is a React SPA with no server-rendered records, so DOM scraping returns nothing. Uses advancedsearch.php?output=json instead. extract() is async and returns
  Promise<NormalizedRow[]>; the userscript must call SmartTable.render() from .then(). Uses GM_xmlhttpRequest when available to bypass cross-origin restrictions.

  brucebase.js — splits #page-content children on <hr> elements into per-event blocks, then finds the heading <p> by requiring both a[name] and strong a[href]. Setlist paragraphs are stored as string[] (one
  per <p>, stops at the first non-P element), making the column genuinely collapsible. Resource icons are found by alt^="00" which is Wikidot's icon naming convention.

** write the CSS styles file

write the CSS styles file

#+begin_example
Committed (88455e4). A few design decisions worth noting:

  Scoping — .st-wrapper * { box-sizing: border-box; margin: 0; padding: 0 } gives a clean slate inside the wrapper without touching anything on the host page. The trigger button (.st-btn-trigger) lives outside
  the wrapper so it gets its own explicit font/size resets.

  Z-index layering — .st-thead gets z-index: 10 for sticky header, .st-dropdown gets z-index: 9999. The dropdown is appended inside .st-wrapper which has position: relative but no z-index, so it doesn't create
  a competing stacking context — the 9999 value beats everything.

  st-shading-changed — uses !important on background-color only, which is the one case where it's justified: the class is transient (removed after the CSS transition completes) and must override both
  .st-tr:nth-child(even) .st-td and .st-tr:hover .st-td.

  Auto-inject guard — document.getElementById('st-styles') prevents double-injection if the library is @required twice (e.g. by two userscripts on the same page).

  /* css */ hint — the tagged template comment on the STYLES export is recognised by CSS-in-JS tools and VS Code's CSS extension for syntax highlighting inside the template literal.

** write the GitHub Actions release workflow

write the GitHub Actions release workflow

#+begin_example
Done (83500c1). The workflow has two design decisions worth explaining:

  The "verify dist" guard (step 5) — The workflow rebuilds from source and then diffs the result against what was committed. If they differ, the run fails with a clear fix instruction. This enforces that
  dist/smarttable.min.js is always the honest output of its source at that tag — no stale or hand-edited bundles can sneak through. esbuild is byte-for-byte deterministic given the same source + lockfile, so a
  correctly-built dist always passes.

  Why no auto-commit of dist — Some workflows rebuild and force-push the artifact back into the tag. That approach creates a mutable tag, which breaks jsDelivr's CDN cache (the CDN sees the tag hash change and
  may serve stale content). Keeping the dist committed at tag time and verifying it in CI gives a stable, cache-friendly CDN URL without any tag mutation.

  Release checklist for shipping a version:
  # 1. Update version in package.json
  # 2. Rebuild
  npm run build
  # 3. Commit both
  git add package.json dist/smarttable.min.js
  git commit -m "Release v1.1.0"
  # 4. Tag — workflow fires automatically
  git tag v1.1.0
  git push origin main --tags
#+end_example

** complete the table-renderer.js ResizeEngine integration

complete the table-renderer.js ResizeEngine integration

#+begin_example
Done. Here's a summary of every change and why each one was needed:

  resize-engine.js — attach() calls _applyWidths()
  The original attach() called _ensureColgroup() which creates brand-new <col> elements, then stopped. Those new elements had no widths written to them, so every _rerender() would silently reset all column
  widths to auto. The fix: one extra _applyWidths() call at the end of attach(). It's a no-op on first attach (empty widths map) and restores stored widths on every subsequent re-attach.

  table-renderer.js — four wiring sites:

  ┌───────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │       Site        │                                                       What was missing                                                        │
  ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ _buildWrapper()   │ resize.attach() — engine was constructed but never told which table to manage                                                 │
  ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ _buildWrapper()   │ Initial-width seeding via setColWidth() — col.width values sat unused (and the old th.style.width path violated invariant #3) │
  ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ _buildGlobalBar() │ "Auto-size columns" button — constant BTN_AUTO_RESIZE was defined but the button was never created                            │
  ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ _buildTh()        │ attachDragHandlers() — without this, the drag state machine was wired to document events but no <th> ever triggered them      │
  ├───────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ _rerender()       │ resize.attach() — after thead replacement, the colgroup was gone; re-attaching rebuilds it and re-applies stored widths       │
  └───────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#+end_example

Here's exactly what's needed:

  1. Write the userscript

  Create a file jungleland.user.js with this content (replace {owner} with your GitHub username):

  // ==UserScript==
  // @name         Jungleland Smart Table
  // @namespace    smarttable-lib
  // @version      0.1
  // @match        https://www.jungleland.it/html/list.htm
  // @require      https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{owner}/smarttable-lib/main/dist/smarttable.min.js
  // @require      https://raw.githubusercontent.com/{owner}/smarttable-lib/main/adapters/jungleland.js
  // @grant        none
  // ==/UserScript==

  const container = document.querySelector(JunglelandAdapter.triggerSelector);
  if (container) {
      SmartTable.render({
          columns:   JunglelandAdapter.columnDefs,
          rows:      JunglelandAdapter.extract(),
          container,
      });
  }

  raw.githubusercontent.com works immediately from the push — no release tag needed. Switch to a pinned jsDelivr URL (@1.0.0) once you've verified it works.

  2. Install in Tampermonkey

  Tampermonkey → Dashboard → + (New Script) → paste → Ctrl+S.

  3. Visit the page

  Go to https://www.jungleland.it/html/list.htm. You should see a Show table button appear next to the search form (form[name="theForm"]). Click it.

  ---
  One known limitation to watch for

  The href column will render as plain URL text, not a clickable link. _makeSubrow uses .textContent, never .innerHTML (XSS rule). There's no render callback on ColumnDef yet — that would be the fix if you
  want live links. For a first test it's fine; you can still see the URL.

  Tampermonkey @require cache

  Tampermonkey caches remote @require files. If you push a fix and the old version keeps loading, open Tampermonkey → script editor → check for updates, or temporarily append ?v=2 to the URL to bust the cache.
#+end_example

* DONE question regarding using claude code "/plan" on one machine and later switching to a different machine to continue working on the same session, what is the best practice ?

Question regarding using claude code "/plan" on one machine and later switching to a different machine to continue
working on the same session, what is the best practice ?

Should I transfer specific files from the "~/.claude" directory or other ones between machines before continuing on the
second ?

#+begin_example
● Here's what I found on session continuity across machines:

  Session storage: Transcripts live at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl, where <project> is your working directory's absolute path with non-alphanumeric chars replaced by dashes. It's tied to that exact path string — if the path differs between machines, the
  session lands in a different <project> folder and won't show up under /resume.

  Manually copying files: Not an officially supported workflow. claude --resume <session-id> is documented to search the current project + worktrees, then other projects on that machine — it isn't described as looking elsewhere. You could try dropping the .jsonl into the
  equivalent path on machine 2, but there's no guarantee, and it's not the sanctioned path.

  Plan mode specifically: Not stored separately — it's just conversation state, but the mode itself (plan, and also bypassPermissions) is explicitly never restored on resume. You'll need to hit Shift+Tab / /plan again after resuming to re-enter plan mode; the plan discussion
  content itself does come back with the rest of the transcript.

  What else matters:

  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                 File                                  │                                 Sync?                                  │
  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .claude/settings.json (project, git-tracked)                          │ Yes — travels with the repo                                            │
  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ .claude/settings.local.json (project, gitignored)                     │ No — machine-specific, leave it                                        │
  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ ~/.claude/settings.json (user/global)                                 │ No — manual only, and gets overridden by project-level settings anyway │
  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ ~/.claude/keybindings.json                                            │ No — machine-specific                                                  │
  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ (auto-memory, used in this repo) │ No — local per machine, not documented as exportable                   │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Recommended approach instead of copying ~/.claude files by hand:
  1. Note the session ID and try claude --resume <session-id> in the same project path on machine 2 (works reliably within the same repo/worktree).
  2. If you're on the Claude web/desktop app rather than pure CLI, those sessions sync automatically via your account.
  3. For pure code handoff, just push/pull via git — the plan's actual output (files, diffs) travels that way regardless of session state.
  4. If neither fits, the pragmatic move is: capture the plan text itself before switching machines, then paste it back in as context on a fresh session — more reliable than fighting path/session-hash mismatches.

  Given this repo already uses the auto-memory system, one option worth considering: ask me to save key decisions from the plan as a project memory before you switch — that at least survives on whichever machine holds this repo's memory directory, even if the raw session doesn't
  transfer.
#+end_example

    at JSON.stringify (<anonymous>)

#+end_example

● I'll investigate the saveTableDataToDisk function to understand why JSON.stringify is failing on this page.

● Explore(Explore saveTableDataToDisk function)
  ⎿  Backgrounded agent (↓ to manage · ctrl+o to expand)

● I've launched an Explore agent to dig into saveTableDataToDisk, its data source, and any existing patterns for handling large data (compression, chunking, etc.). I'll report back once it completes.

✻ Waiting for 1 background agent to finish

● Agent "Explore saveTableDataToDisk function" finished · 2m 23s

● Diagnosis

  The error is a genuine JS engine limit, not a bug in the sense of wrong logic. Here's the chain:

  - saveTableDataToDisk() (ShowAllEntityData.user.js:43311-43516) builds one big JS object from allRows/groupedRows — arrays that accumulate every row from every fetched page (not just what's rendered), storing full cell HTML (via getCleanCellHtml) per cell, not lean scalar values.
  - At line 43490 it does one JSON.stringify(dataToSave, null, 2) call over the whole thing.
  - For an area's /events sub-tab with a large number of linked events, that single string can exceed V8's max string length (~512MB), throwing RangeError: Invalid string length.
  - Gzip compression (pako.gzip, line 43494) happens after the string is built — it does nothing to prevent this, since the crash happens during JSON.stringify itself, before compression ever runs.
  - The , null, 2 pretty-print indentation also inflates the string size unnecessarily (indentation/newlines on every field) before compression.
  - This is very likely the same code path as the "Large Dataset Fetched → 💾 Save to Disk" escape hatch (sa_render_threshold, default 5000 rows) — a user with a huge events list routes straight to save-to-disk without ever rendering, which is exactly the scenario most likely to overflow the string limit.

  There are two independent contributing factors (both real, not mutually exclusive): 1) the JSON is built as one monolithic string with no chunking, and 2) pretty-print indentation inflates that string further. A full fix addresses (1); a quick fix only mitigates via (2) plus a clearer error message.

 ☐ Fix scope

How much do you want to invest in fixing this — a permanent fix or a quick mitigation?

2.)

I want the following implemented, but in a new branch:

#+begin_example
❯ 1. Full streaming/chunked rewrite (Recommended)
     Rewrite saveTableDataToDisk to build the JSON payload in chunks and stream-compress with pako's chunked Deflate API instead of one giant JSON.stringify + gzip call. Eliminates the failure mode entirely, no matter how large the dataset gets. More invasive — touches the core save logic and needs careful testing
     with a large dataset.
#+end_example

*** plan

What tooltip/icon mechanism should this use? The script has two existing patterns: a lightweight emoji+native-title span (used for CAA/EAA cache-hint icons), and a heavier custom floating-div tooltip system (used for the Relationships column).

❯ 1. Lightweight emoji + native title (Recommended)
     A small ⚠️/❌ span appended after the artist's <li> content, tooltip via the native `title` attribute. Matches the existing `.mb-art-cache-hint-col` pattern, minimal new code, no new CSS/JS singleton needed.
  1. Rich floating tooltip
     Reuse the `data-mbtt` + singleton floating-div system used by the Relationships column. Heavier to wire up but allows richer HTML tooltip content (e.g. showing both dates side by side, formatted).

*** explanation

#+begin_example
● Confirmed. Here's the explanation:

  Root cause

  The new name:/comment:/alias: "Cell structure" feature reuses _findCellEntityRefs() (line 16090) for entity discovery — deliberately, per the plan, so it wouldn't re-derive anchor-finding logic that already existed. That function only recognizes an anchor as an "entity
  reference" if its href's first path segment is one of six types listed in _ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH (line 16096-16097):

  const glyphClass = m && _ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH[m[1]];
  if (!glyphClass) return;   // href type not recognized → skip this anchor entirely

  const _ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH = {
      work: 'worklink', place: 'placelink', area: 'arealink',
      artist: 'artistlink', label: 'labellink', event: 'eventlink'
  };

  That map's own doc comment (line 32481-32496) confirms this is a pre-existing, deliberate scope limit, not something new I introduced: it only covers "the 6 types with an already-VERIFIED glyph class precedent in this codebase," and explicitly calls out
  recording/release/release-group/series/instrument as not yet included, "none does today" — it predates the name/comment/alias feature entirely (it was built for release-tracks' AR-column header glyphs).

  Since _findCellEntityCommentParts() (my new helper) only ever iterates over whatever _findCellEntityRefs() returns, it inherited this exact same six-type restriction as a side effect:

  - /artist/.../releases "Release" column — links are /release/<mbid> → release isn't in the map → every anchor is skipped → zero entity refs → zero name/comment/alias entries.
  - /artist/.../recordings "Name" column — links are /recording/<mbid> → recording isn't in the map → same result.
  - /artist/.../relationships "Title" column — this one shows whichever entity is on the other end of each relationship, so it's mixed; it works fine for rows targeting a work/event/etc., but any row whose target is a release/recording/release-group gets skipped the same way. For
  this specific artist's relationships list, the visible rows are apparently dominated by types outside the six, so nothing shows up in that column's dropdown either.

  By contrast, the original "Work"/"Authors" example worked because work and artist are both in the map.

  This is exactly why the doc comment describes it as "a one-line addition whenever a verified glyph class exists" for a new type — extending _ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH to include release/recording/etc. would fix all three, but that map is also used elsewhere (release-tracks
  column-header glyphs), so adding a type there is a shared, not fully isolated, change. Let me know if you'd like me to implement that extension.
#+end_example

*** findings

#+begin_example
● The snapshots are decisive — and they overturn something I said earlier.

  Key finding

  debug/mb-icons.css actually defines .recordinglink and .releaselink as real, styled classes:

  grep -oE "\.[a-zA-Z-]*link\b" mb-icons.css | sort -u
  .arealink .artistlink .collectionlink .eventlink .genrelink .instrumentlink
  .labellink .placelink .recordinglink .releaselink .rglink .serieslink .taglink .worklink

  Your rec-rel.html/rel-rel.html snapshots confirm MusicBrainz actually emits them live: <span class="recordinglink"></span> and <span class="releaselink"></span> sit right before the anchor on the relationships page's "Title" column.

  This means the existing code's own comment ("no recordinglink/releaselink… class exists anywhere in this file or in real MusicBrainz markup") is simply wrong/outdated — it was written without having checked this specific page shape. That comment was the entire basis for my
  "Option B, avoid touching the shared map" recommendation last time, since I was worried extending it would attach a glyph class with nothing behind it. That worry is gone: .releaselink/.recordinglink are real, already-styled classes, exactly matching the "trust the host page's
  stylesheet" contract the other six types already rely on.

  Revised recommendation

  Option A (extend the shared _ENTITY_TYPE_GLYPH map) is now the right call, not Option B. Concretely: add
  release:   'releaselink',
  recording: 'recordinglink',
  Two entries — that's all that's needed. Checking it against all six originally-broken cases:

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬───────────┐
  │                  URL / column                   │ entity type behind the link │ fixed by  │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼───────────┤
  │ artist/releases "Release"                       │ release                     │ release   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼───────────┤
  │ artist/relationships "Title" (rec-rel/work-rel) │ recording                   │ recording │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼───────────┤
  │ artist/relationships "Title" (rel-rel)          │ release                     │ release   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼───────────┤
  │ artist/recordings "Name"                        │ recording                   │ recording │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼───────────┤
  │ label "Release"                                 │ release                     │ release   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼───────────┤
  │ series "Release"                                │ release                     │ release   │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼───────────┤
  │ instrument/releases "Release"                   │ release                     │ release   │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴───────────┘

  All six are release/recording-typed — none of them actually need series/instrument/release-group/etc. themselves (those URLs are pages about a series/instrument, but the "Release" column there links to releases, not back to the series/instrument). The stylesheet also confirms
  real classes for serieslink/instrumentlink/rglink/collectionlink/genrelink if you ever want those too, but they're not needed for what you reported.

  No breakage risk either way now — it's purely additive to the six already-recognized types, and the new glyph markers will render correctly (real CSS backing) rather than the blank-icon scenario I was worried about last time.
#+end_example

  What changed on pull: commit b24f3bc ("fix: unique-values dropdown flag/area icons bunched at start...") reworked flag/area-icon rendering inside renderItems()/flagIconMap — a different part of the same openUniqDrop() function, unrelated to synBox/"Cell structure"/quick-filter

  _sortedNameValues/_sortedAliasValues dedup sites all still exist with identical structure — just at new line numbers, which I've updated in the plan. I also confirmed the one remaining unpulled remote commit (098d2ea) only touches README.org and is irrelevant. debug/uvd.html is

● User approved Claude's plan
  ⎿  Plan saved to: ~/.claude/plans/debug-uvd-html-complete-unique-wondrous-lemon.md · /plan to edit
     Unique-Value Dropdown (UVD): sectioned, collapsible "Cell structure", smarter quick filter

     ▎ Note: line numbers below were re-verified against the current branch
     ▎ tip (commit b24f3bc, pulled from another machine after the original
     ▎ exploration) — that commit reworked flag/area-icon rendering inside
     ▎ renderItems()/flagIconMap (lines ~42816-43370 in the pre-pull file),
     ▎ shifting everything from synBox onward by ~+95-140 lines. It does not
     ▎ touch synBox/"Cell structure"/quick-filter code, so none of the
     ▎ structural analysis or approach below changed — only the absolute line
     ▎ numbers were refreshed.

     Context

     openUniqDrop() (ShowAllEntityData.user.js:42370-44231) builds the per-column
     "unique value" filter dropdown (📊 button in each sortable column header). On
     the debug/uvd.html snapshot (Artist column, /instrument/…/artists), the
     panel renders 597 rows in one scroll area: a synBox region with 196
     items all crammed under a single "Cell structure" header, followed by a flat
     401-item alphabetical listBox. The "Cell structure" header currently hides
     up to 9 unrelated families of synthetic entries with no sub-grouping:
     structural states (empty/single/collapsed/expanded/any), flags (≠ track/rec.
     mismatch, ~ name-variation), artwork presence (✓/✗), five credit-value
     families (attribute/task/date/instrument/credited-as), three entity-info
     families (name/comment/alias), and event roles — plus the already-separate
     "Relationship icons" and inline-artwork mini-sections. This makes the panel
     overwhelming and makes same-looking values appear 2-3 times (once as a plain
     whole-cell row, once as an entity-glyph href row, once as a "» name:"
     structure-mode row) with no visual explanation of why.

     The user wants (discussed and agreed):
     1. Reduce look-alike duplication without removing real functionality.
     2. Break "Cell structure" into named, independently collapsible sections with
     icons/glyphs, mirroring the multi-section idea already partially present
     (Relationship icons / inline-artwork already get their own header).
     3. Keep the single existing global quick filter (already covers listBox and
     most of synBox) rather than adding N per-section filter boxes — but make
     it smarter: auto-reveal matches inside collapsed sections, and close the
     existing gap where it doesn't filter "Relationship icons" entries at all.

     Decisions already made with the user (see prior AskUserQuestion):
     - Global quick filter only, made smarter — no per-section filter inputs.
     - Section collapse/expand state is remembered globally by section name
     (not per-column), persisted across dropdown opens.
     - Suppress "» name:"/"» alias:" synthetic entries when that exact text is
     already independently selectable elsewhere in the same dropdown (as a
     plain whole-cell value, or as an entity-glyph href row) — only genuinely
     new information keeps its own row.
     - The main "All values" list (listBox) stays always-expanded; only the
     synthetic synBox sections become collapsible.

     Approach

     1. Introduce a section-container abstraction inside synBox

     Currently every builder (makeSynItem, makeValueSynItem, makeInlineArtItem,
     the inline "Relationship icons" block starting at 43850) appends its item
     <div> directly as a sibling of synBox, with plain header <div>s and
     appendSynDivider() calls in between (43490-43948). Replace this with a
     small registry keyed by section name:

     const _synSections = new Map(); // key -> { wrapper, itemsBox, headerEl }
     function getOrCreateSynSection(key, label, glyph) { ... }

     getOrCreateSynSection lazily creates, on first use, a
     <div class="mb-uniq-section"> containing:
     - <div class="mb-uniq-section-hdr" role="button" tabindex="0"> — a ▶/▼
     toggle glyph + glyph icon + label text + (later) a match-count badge —
     click/Enter toggles the section (see §3 for persistence).
     - <div class="mb-uniq-section-items" role="group"> — the actual item rows,
     same children makeSynItem/makeValueSynItem/etc. already build today,
     just appended here instead of directly to synBox.

     Proposed section keys/labels/glyphs (grouping the existing families 1:1, no
     new data collection needed — every count/Map already computed at
     42400-42638 and 43475-43492 stays exactly as-is):

     ┌───────────────┬────────────────────┬───────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
     │      key      │       label        │ glyph │                      existing entries moved in                      │
     ├───────────────┼────────────────────┼───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ structure     │ Structure          │ 🔠    │ empty/single/collapsed/expanded/any, artwork ✓/✗, inline-art yes/no │
     ├───────────────┼────────────────────┼───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ flags         │ Flags              │ 🚩    │ title-mismatch ≠, name-variation ~                                  │
     ├───────────────┼────────────────────┼───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ credit        │ Credit details     │ 🎚️    │ attr/task/date/instrument/altname                                   │
     ├───────────────┼────────────────────┼───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ entity        │ Entity info        │ 👤    │ name/comment/alias (post-dedup, see §2)                             │
     ├───────────────┼────────────────────┼───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ roles         │ Roles              │ 🎭    │ event role                                                          │
     ├───────────────┼────────────────────┼───────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
     │ relationships │ Relationship icons │ 🔗    │ existing per-domain favicon rows                                    │
     └───────────────┴────────────────────┴───────┴─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

     Call sites to update: makeSynItem/makeValueSynItem/makeInlineArtItem
     gain a sectionKey argument (or infer it from mode/kind — simplest is an
     explicit argument since callers already know their family); the section
     build blocks at 43729-43807 (collapsable-column "Cell structure" branch),
     43808-43844 (non-collapsable-column branch), 43850-43938 (Relationship
     icons), 43939-43971 (inline thumbnail presence) route their
     synBox.appendChild(item) calls through getOrCreateSynSection(key, ...).itemsBox
     instead. Remove the now-redundant standalone synHdr/appendSynDivider()
     calls — the section wrapper supplies its own header and visual separation
     (a border-top on .mb-uniq-section + .mb-uniq-section, CSS-only).

     2. Entity-info dedup ("only show when it adds info")

     At 43805/43807 (_sortedNameValues.forEach / _sortedAliasValues.forEach,
     also mirrored at 43840/43842 in the non-collapsable-column branch): before
     calling makeValueSynItem('name', v, …) / makeValueSynItem('alias', v, …),
     skip v when it's already independently selectable elsewhere in the same
     panel — i.e. v is already a key in valueCounts (a plain whole-cell value)
     or already present as an entityInfo name for an href kept in combinedVals
     (an entity-glyph row). Build one small Set of "already-offered bare names"
     right after combinedVals is assembled (42659-42663) and reuse it at both
     name/alias filter sites. » comment: entries are untouched — a
     disambiguation comment is never independently selectable any other way, so
     there's no redundancy to remove there.

     3. Collapse/expand + persistence

     - New CSS classes: .mb-uniq-section, .mb-uniq-section-hdr (clickable,
     same visual language as the existing "Cell structure" header font:
     font-size:0.75em; font-weight:600; color:#555; letter-spacing:0.03em,
     plus cursor:pointer and a ▶/▼ prefix), .mb-uniq-section-items
     (display:none when collapsed). Add near the existing .mb-col-uniq-syn-box
     CSS block (~`27766-27881`).
     - Persist collapse state with GM_setValue/GM_getValue, following the
     existing non-configSchema UI-state pattern already used for column
     visibility (ShowAllEntityData.user.js:17149/17162) and dropdown geometry
     (29792/29812) — a single JSON object under one new key, e.g.
     mb_sa_uniq_section_collapse, shaped { structure: false, credit: true, … }
     (missing key = expanded, the current always-expanded behavior, so first-run
     users see no change). Read once when openUniqDrop builds the panel, write
     on every header click.
     - Header click toggles itemsBox display, flips the ▶/▼ glyph, and persists
     the new state for that section key globally (shared across every column —
     per the user's decision, not scoped per-column).

     4. Smarter global quick filter

     - Fix the coverage gap: give the "Relationship icons" section's item rows a
     dataset.mbUniqSynLabel + .mb-uniq-syn-label-text span the same way
     _appendSynLabelText() already does for every other synBox entry
     (43555-43561), instead of the bespoke lbl span built inline in that
     block — this alone makes _applySynBoxQuickFilter() (44010-44046)
     cover them for free, no separate filter logic needed.
     - In _applySynBoxQuickFilter(filter), after computing each item's
     matches, additionally: (a) track a per-section match count as items are
     visited (Array.from(synBox.children) becomes a walk over each section's
     itemsBox children instead, or an outer loop over _synSections), (b)
     force a section's itemsBox visible (ignoring its persisted collapsed
     state) whenever it has ≥1 match while filter is non-empty, restoring the
     persisted collapsed/expanded state when filter is cleared, and (c) render
     the match count in the section header, e.g. Credit details (3), while
     filtering (revert to plain label text when the filter is cleared).

     Files touched

     - ShowAllEntityData.user.js — all of the above lives inside/around
     openUniqDrop() (42370-44231) plus the CSS block for .mb-col-uniq-syn-box
     (~27766-27881, unaffected by the recent flag-icon commit since that only
     touched code inside openUniqDrop() itself). Also check the column-header

● User approved Claude's plan
  ⎿  Plan saved to: ~/.claude/plans/1-is-it-possible-moonlit-emerson.md · /plan to edit
     extractMainColumn: split into MB-Name / Comment / MB-Primary alias

     Context

     debug/review-extract-maincolumn.org asked to review extractMainColumn
     (the feature that splits a page's main entity column, e.g. 'Work'/'Event',
     into synthetic MB-Name + Comment columns) now that this session already
     built a generic name/comment/primary-alias splitter for list-style entity
     cells (_findCellEntityRefs() / _findCellEntityCommentParts()).

     Investigation (reading the actual code + debug/work-comment-bug.html,
     debug/place-events-original.html/-final.html) confirmed the bug reported
     in the org file: extractMainColumn's "Comment" extraction never strips
     <i title="Primary alias"> before reading the comment text, so on a row
     whose entity comment is wholly or partly a primary alias (e.g. artist-works'
     "An der schönen blauen Donau, op. 314" → alias "On the Beautiful Blue
     Danube, op. 314"), the "Comment" column silently shows the alias text
     mislabeled as a disambiguation comment.

     The extraction logic is duplicated almost verbatim at exactly two call
     sites in startFetchingProcess() (~line 36107-36175, the artist-releasegroups
     branch, and ~line 36828-36905, the generic else-branch) — both build tdName/
     tdComment by hand, neither ever looks for i[title="Primary alias"].

     A second, independent code path has the identical root-cause bug:
     _tagCountBase() (line 2686, backing Name_Comment, Name_Date_Comment,
     Name_Comment_Artists, tagCount_Name_Comment, tagCount_Name_Date_Comment,
     tagCount_Name_Comment_Artists — used by tag-value/tag-count/user-tag-value
     page types via columnExtractors, not extractMainColumn) also reads
     .comment bdi's raw textContent with no alias stripping.

     Separately, ColumnDataExtractor.primaryAlias (line 3528) is an existing
     DOM-mutating extractor (columnExtractors pipeline) that already solves
     this correctly today, by removing <i title="Primary alias"> from the
     source cell (and cleaning up the orphaned leading ", ") before
     extractMainColumn's Comment read ever runs. Cross-referencing every
     extractor: 'primaryAlias' usage against its page definition's
     extractMainColumn value shows:
     - 7 usages target the exact same source column as their own
     extractMainColumn (confirmed directly: place-events's Events block —
     sourceColumn: 'Event' / extractMainColumn: 'Event'; another Events
     block — sourceColumn: 'Name' / extractMainColumn: 'Name'; the
     artist-releasegroups Title block — sourceColumn: 'Title' /
     extractMainColumn: 'Title'; plus 4 more of the same shape). Once
     extractMainColumn natively splits out its own alias column, these
     become fully redundant — same data MusicBrainz already renders once,
     extracted twice under two different column names ("Primary Alias" vs the
     new "MB-Primary alias").
     - 3 usages (all sourceColumn: 'Event', entityFeatures 'Events'
     blocks on tag-value-style page types, e.g. lines ~11700-11718,
     ~11780-ish, ~12181-12198) do not use extractMainColumn at all —
     they pair primaryAlias with the _tagCountBase-backed Name_Date_Comment
     extractor instead. These stay as-is; primaryAlias remains their only
     source of alias data.

     Per discussion (see prior turn's AskUserQuestion), scope for this task is:
     fix both code paths, and retire the 7 redundant primaryAlias
     entries that duplicate what the enhanced extractMainColumn will now
     produce natively. The 3 _tagCountBase-paired primaryAlias entries are
     kept untouched.

     Approach

     1. New shared helper: _extractMainColumnParts(targetCell)

     Add next to the two existing inline blocks (~line 36090), replacing their
     duplicated Name/Comment-building code. Keeps the existing Name-extraction
     logic byte-for-byte (no behavior change there — <a><bdi> preferred, then
     first <a>, then first meaningful text node, then full text minus
     .comment). Replaces the Comment-extraction step with an alias-aware split
     mirroring _findCellEntityCommentParts()'s technique (remove the alias
     element first, then read what's left; strip a leftover leading ", "):

     (No paren-stripping needed — MusicBrainz renders the comment's surrounding
     ( ) via CSS ::before/::after, confirmed absent from .textContent in
     the actual debug snapshot; only the literal ", " separator between alias
     and trailing comment text is a real DOM text node.)

     2. Wire the third column into both row-building call sites

     At both ~36107-36175 and ~36828-36905:
     - Replace the inline extraction with a call to _extractMainColumnParts(targetCell).
     - Register primarySyntheticCellMap.set('MB-Primary alias', tdAlias) next to
     the existing MB-Name/Comment registrations (so syntheticColumnExtractors
     can source from it later, consistent with how Comment is already exposed
     to e.g. eventParts).
     - Append newRow.appendChild(tdAlias) next to the existing tdName/tdComment
     appends (~36241-36243 and ~36965-36968), keeping it as the third and last
     of the trio.

     3. Header + tooltip + bookkeeping (cleanupHeaders, ~34459-34523)

     - Add a third <th> block for MB-Primary alias, mirroring the existing
     Comment block (same mb-extracted-column class, headerBgColor,
     idempotent headersText.includes(...) guard).
     - _synthColTooltip()'s 'extractMainColumn' case (~34220-34225): add an
     MB-Primary alias branch (short explanatory sentence, mirroring the
     MB-Name/Comment ones).
     - _resolvedPrimaryCols (~34470-34474): also .add('MB-Primary alias').
     - Header-name tracking array (~35968-35972): also
     _finalColNames.push('MB-Primary alias').

     4. Fix _tagCountBase() (line 2686) the same way

     Replace its raw _commentBdi.textContent read with the same
     remove-the-alias-element-first technique used in _extractMainColumnParts
     (no new synthetic column here — the 3 page blocks that need the alias value
     already get it from their own untouched primaryAlias columnExtractor
     entry; this change only stops it from also leaking into Comment). All 6
     extractor functions built on _tagCountBase (Name_Comment,
     Name_Date_Comment, Name_Comment_Artists, tagCount_Name_Comment,
     tagCount_Name_Date_Comment, tagCount_Name_Comment_Artists) get the fix
     for free since they all destructure tdComment from it.

     5. Retire the 7 redundant primaryAlias entries

     For each page-definition block where extractor: 'primaryAlias''s
     sourceColumn matches that block's own extractMainColumn value:
     - Remove the { sourceColumn: '<X>', extractor: 'primaryAlias', syntheticColumns: ['Primary Alias'] }
     entry from columnExtractors.
     - In that block's tooltipColumns (where present), replace any 'Primary Alias'
     reference with 'MB-Primary alias'.
     - Re-grep -n "extractor: 'primaryAlias'" at implementation time to get the
     authoritative, current line numbers rather than relying on the ones found
     during this investigation (the file shifts as earlier edits land) —
     cross-check each hit's nearest extractMainColumn in the same
     entityFeatures sub-block before removing it, since a naive nearest-match
     scan (tried during investigation) misfires across adjacent sub-blocks in
     this densely-nested region of pageDefinitions.
     - Do not touch the 3 _tagCountBase-paired entries (no sibling
     extractMainColumn in the same block) — leave those primaryAlias
     entries and their 'Primary Alias' synthetic column in place.

     Not in scope

     - No new alias column is added to _tagCountBase-family page blocks that
     currently have neither extractMainColumn nor a paired primaryAlias
     extractor (e.g. plain Name_Comment on Areas/Labels/Places/Release groups
     entityFeatures blocks) — they simply stop leaking the alias into Comment;
     a dedicated alias column for that family would be new-feature scope, not
     a bug fix, and can be a separate follow-up if wanted.
     - ColumnDataExtractor.primaryAlias itself is not deleted — it's still
     needed by the 3 kept usages.

     Files touched

     Only ShowAllEntityData.user.js:
     - New function _extractMainColumnParts() (~line 36090 area)
     - Two row-building call sites (~36107-36243, ~36828-36968)
     - cleanupHeaders() header injection + _synthColTooltip() (~34220-34523)
     - _tagCountBase() (line 2686)
     - 7 pageDefinitions entries (remove redundant primaryAlias columnExtractors
     entries + fix tooltipColumns references)

     2. Load https://musicbrainz.org/artist/70248960-cb53-4ea4-943a-edb18f7d336f/works:

#+begin_example
● Yes, it's feasible — and there's already a working precedent in this codebase doing exactly this shape of thing, for two other synthetic columns.

  Existing template: _suppressReleaseEventsIfNoReleaseLinks(table) and _suppressRelationshipsIfNoReleaseOrReleaseGroupLinks(table) already conditionally remove a column (header <th> + every row's <td> + the
  matching column-filter-row cell) from a table when no row satisfies some condition. Mechanism: guard against an empty tbody (bail out — important, see below), scan all rows for the condition, and if it fails
  everywhere, delete the header cell, every body cell at that index (descending index order), and the corresponding filter-row <input> cell, so thead/tbody/filter-row stay index-aligned.

  Hook point exists in both modes already:
  - Single-table (tableMode: 'single'): called right after cleanupHeaders()/addColumnFilterRow() and before makeTableSortableUnified(), at ShowAllEntityData.user.js:37294 / :37303.
  - Multi-table/grouped (tableMode: 'multi'): called per-subtable inside renderGroupedTable() at :39822 / :39831, also before that subtable's makeTableSortableUnified() call — and since each subtable's header
  is a cloneNode'd (or, for tag-value/user-ratings page types, independently rebuilt) copy, removing the column in one subtable doesn't affect siblings, satisfying "per table/subtable" naturally.

  A new _suppressCommentColumnsIfEmpty(table) (checking "does any row have non-empty Comment / MB-Primary alias text" instead of "does any row link to a release") could be dropped into these same two call
  sites.

  Risks / things to decide before implementing:
  1. Empty-tbody race during re-filtering — runFilter() clears and rebuilds tbody before re-rendering, so the emptiness check must bail out on a currently-empty tbody (the precedent already does this) or it'll
  wrongly strip the column on a transient empty state.
  2. Column can appear/disappear as the user filters/sorts, since suppression re-evaluates on every re-render. This is already accepted behavior for Release events/Relationships today, not a new risk class —
  but worth confirming you're OK with Comment/MB-Primary alias doing the same.
  3. Found a real existing gap while checking this: the disk-cache-restore render path (:50720-50725) does not call either suppression function before wiring sort, unlike the normal fetch-and-render path
  (:37294-:37305). So today, Release events/Relationships suppression is already inconsistently applied depending on whether a page loads fresh or from the IndexedDB cache. A new Comment/MB-Primary-alias
  suppression would either inherit this same gap or need a third call site added to fix it properly.
  4. Persisted multi-sort state (multiTableSortStates, keyed by raw column index) could theoretically point at a stale index if a column's presence flips between re-renders — an accepted, pre-existing risk
  class the current precedent already lives with, not something new.
  5. Config safety is fine: tooltipColumns, collapsableColumns, integerColumns all resolve columns by name and gracefully skip if missing (no crash) — including the 'MB-Primary alias'/'italic:Comment'
  references already added to several page definitions in the last commit.

  So: architecturally sound, low-risk, and it'd reuse an established pattern rather than invent a new one. Want me to implement it (and should it also fix the cache-restore gap for consistency, or leave that
  alone)?
#+end_example

** explanation

#+begin_example
 Explanation: is collapsableColumns: [ 'CAA' ] / [ 'EAA' ] actually needed?

 This is a research/explanation deliverable, not an implementation plan — per your
 request, no code has been changed. Findings below, with exact line numbers in
 ShowAllEntityData.user.js.

 Short answer

 There are two completely separate, independently-wired collapse/expand systems
 for CAA/EAA columns, and only one of them actually works:

 1. The dedicated CAA/EAA system — .mb-caa-col-hdr-btn/.mb-eaa-col-hdr-btn
 (the icon+thumbnail button, debug/CAA-collapse-toggle.html). Built by
 _artInitCaaColHeaderToggle() (lines 59528-59674), called from the tail of
 initCaaPics()/initEaaPics(). Gated only on sa_enable_caa_pics/
 sa_enable_eaa_pics and "does this table have a CAA/EAA column" —
 it does not read collapsableColumns at all. This is the one that
 actually collapses/expands the images (via [data-caa-expand-btn] clicks
 routed through ensureCollapseDelegate()'s dedicated CAA branch,
 lines 46227-46278).
 2. The generic collapsableColumns system — .mb-col-collapse-hdr-btn
 (the ▶/count/▤ button, debug/normal-collapse-button.html). Built by
 initCollapsableColumns() (lines 46598-47290) for any column named in
 features.collapsableColumns. For CAA/EAA columns this button is
 either missing or present-but-completely-inert — see below. It never
 successfully collapses/expands a CAA/EAA cell.

 So: for its apparent purpose (driving expand/collapse), collapsableColumns: ['CAA']/['EAA'] is not needed — that job is already done, correctly and
 independently, by system #1. But it is not entirely side-effect-free to remove
 — see "Before removing anything" below.

 Why the generic button is broken for CAA/EAA (root cause)

 _findCellListItems()/_classifyCollapseCell() (lines 16898-16927,
 17194-17204) are purely structural — they match any <ul>/<ol> in a cell, with
 no CAA/EAA awareness at all. Once _artBuildMultiRowArtCell() (lines
 57173-57317) has built a cell's ul.mb-caa-art-ul > li.mb-caa-art-li-summary + li.mb-caa-art-li-image×N, _findCellListItems() happily matches it as a
 qualifying "multi-row list cell" — exactly like a Producer/Instruments cell.

 initCollapsableColumns() deliberately still counts these cells toward
 multiRowCells/its header button's existence and displayed count (explicit
 comment at lines 46804-46812: doing so is enough to "drive
 anyColumnHasMultiRow → column-header button creation" since "the header
 button's click handler finds and clicks their existing toggles"). That
 assumption is stale: as part of the CAA/EAA rework, _artBuildMultiRowArtCell()
 stopped injecting .mb-cell-collapse-toggle into art cells at all — its
 own doc comment (57148-57152) says so explicitly, replacing it with
 [data-caa-expand-btn]. But every click handler in the generic system
 (the per-column header button, the global "expand all" button, and
 _applyCollapseState() itself) only ever looks for .mb-cell-collapse-toggle
 — which no longer exists on these cells. So clicking the generic button
 silently does nothing to CAA/EAA cells: no error, just inert.

 Why it's missing on one page and present (but dead) on the other — matches your two fixtures exactly

 - initCollapsableColumns() runs synchronously, immediately during
 renderFinalTable()/renderGroupedTable().
 - CAA/EAA images are fetched asynchronously — initCaaPics()/initEaaPics()
 enqueue network/IDB work that eventually calls _artBuildMultiRowArtCell()
 well after the synchronous render pass finishes.
 - debug/CAA-without-collapse-symbol.html (fresh render of the "Performed
 release" sub-table, a multi-table page): initCollapsableColumns() ran
 before any cell had a ul.mb-caa-art-ul yet → zero cells counted → the
 generic button was never created at all (matches: no
 .mb-col-collapse-hdr-btn in that snippet).
 - debug/CAA-with-collapse-symbol.html (the same table re-rendered as a
 "Show single-table" cross-tab snapshot): captureSubtableSnapshot() captures
 getCleanCellHtml(cell) from the source tab — by the time you actually click
 "Show single-table", the async CAA fetch has almost always already finished,
 so the captured HTML already contains the built <ul>. When the new tab
 hydrates and its own initCollapsableColumns() runs, it now finds 4
 qualifying cells → builds the button, showing "Expand ALL multi-row CAA cells (4)" — but clicking it is a no-op, for the reason above.
 (This isn't unique to cross-tab hydration — any re-render that happens to
 run after the async art build completes, e.g. a later filter/sort, would
 reproduce the same "present but dead" state on the original page too.)

 Is it "needed"? — nuanced

 Not needed for expand/collapse — that's fully covered by the separate,
 always-correctly-wired CAA-specific system regardless of what
 collapsableColumns says.

 But not provably side-effect-free to remove, because _classifyCollapseCell/
 _findCellListItems — the same functions that (mis)drive the dead button —
 are also the shared source of truth for other features documented in
 CLAUDE.md, all scoped to columns declared in collapsableColumns:
 - _updateAllColHeaderCounts() (.mb-col-collapse-count bookkeeping)
 - _syncCollapseHasMatchInTable() — which has its own explicit CAA/EAA-aware
 "Pass 2" branch (lines 17456-17474), suggesting someone did intend
 CAA/EAA to participate in at least this part of the generic system
 - openUniqDrop()'s "Cell structure" empty/single/multi-row counts and
 structure-mode column filters
 - testRowMatch()'s multi-row column filter matching (per CLAUDE.md's own
 note that _classifyCollapseCell is "the single source of truth" these all
 route through)

 I have not yet confirmed whether these are scoped strictly to columns
 literally listed in collapsableColumns (in which case removing 'CAA'/'EAA'
 would also silently drop "filter by cells with multiple images" / structure
 counts for that column, alongside removing the dead button), or whether they
 run for CAA/EAA columns unconditionally regardless of this config. That's the
 one open question worth resolving before touching anything.

 Suggested next step (not yet done — just naming the option)

 If you want to proceed, the natural follow-up would be a short, targeted
 investigation of exactly that gating question (does initCollapsableColumns's
 activeCollapsableColumns scoping also gate _updateAllColHeaderCounts/
 _syncCollapseHasMatchInTable/openUniqDrop's structure filters for a column,
 or are those independent), so any removal of 'CAA'/'EAA' from the 21
 collapsableColumns arrays that list it can be scoped correctly — e.g. maybe
 the dead generic button should simply be suppressed specifically for CAA/EAA
 columns (skip building .mb-col-collapse-hdr-btn for them) while keeping the
 rest of the classification/filtering machinery intact, rather than removing
 the collapsableColumns declaration outright.
#+end_example

Root cause: the cross-tab snapshot handoff deliberately does not capture the async-populated `mb-rel-cell` data cells (they're meant to be freshly (re)built post-hydration by cleanupHeaders()/initRelationshipsColumn(), gated on the *destination* page definition's `features.injectedColumns`) — but `artist-relationships-filtered` (the tableMode:'single' definition the `?link_type_id=1`-qualified snapshot tab routes to) never declared `injectedColumns: ['Relationships']` in the first place, unlike its multi-table sibling `artist-relationships` and unlike the equivalent `label-relationships-filtered`/`place-performances-filtered` definitions (which already had it and were unaffected). With no active injected-column descriptor, cleanupHeaders()'s unconditional \"always remove foreign Relationships/Release events/Tagger header text\" pass still deleted the plain-text \"Relationships\" `<th>` that came along in the captured header HTML, but its later re-injection step (gated on the same descriptor) never ran to replace it, and initRelationshipsColumn() bailed immediately — so neither the header nor any `mb-rel-cell` `<td>` was ever (re)created. Added the missing `injectedColumns: ['Relationships']` declaration to `artist-relationships-filtered`."
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
#+end_example

#+begin_example

● I've updated the plan file with the full sizing analysis. Summary:

  The biggest lever isn't cloneNode — it's _updateAllColHeaderCounts. The code itself documents this O(rows×columns) per-column count scan as taking "30-120s for 8k+ rows" (that's why it's already deferred via
  setTimeout(0) rather than fixed). Scaled to 5,000 rows, that's ~19-75s of background work re-triggered on every filter keystroke, every sort, every global expand/collapse-all click, and every multi-table
  render — because initCollapsableColumns() (which schedules it) is called from all of those sites.

  Two new areas beyond what we discussed last time:
  - Sort pays the same tax Fix C removes from filter. The branch's WIP.1 only touched runFilter(); applying a sort still calls renderFinalTable(allRows) → full rebuild → the same expensive header-count scan.
  Same fix, different trigger site, not yet done anywhere.
  - The header-count scan itself has zero caching, independent of what triggers it — even after fixing filter and sort, global collapse/expand-all clicks and multi-table renders would still force a full
  recompute.

  Rough sizing for a 5,000-row/~20-column table (estimates from operation-count analysis against the code's own documented cost baseline, not live profiling):

  ┌─────┬─────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  #  │                 Fix                 │            Est. improvement            │
  ├─────┼─────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 1   │ Fix C (filter)                      │ 95-99% per-keystroke                   │
  ├─────┼─────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 2   │ Same fix, extended to Sort          │ 90-99% per-sort-click                  │
  ├─────┼─────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 3   │ Cache _updateAllColHeaderCounts     │ 90%+ on toggle/multi-table triggers    │
  ├─────┼─────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 4   │ openUniqDrop() caching              │ 90-98% on repeat opens                 │
  ├─────┼─────────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 5   │ Lazy CAA/EAA (IntersectionObserver) │ ~99% fewer initial art requests queued │
  └─────┴─────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Recommended order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5. The first four share one theme ("stop re-scanning everything on every action") and build on the same caching/invalidation primitive, so doing them in sequence compounds
  the wins; #5 is an independent subsystem (artwork/network) and can slot in anytime.
#+end_example

** a

#+begin_example

  1) Should we /clear then do each step?
  Yes, that's a good pattern here. This file is 63.5k lines and we've already burned a fair amount of context just analyzing it. Since the plan is fully written to disk (not dependent on conversation memory),
  each step can start clean: /clear → fresh session → point it at the plan file → implement just that one item. Keeps each step focused and avoids drift from unrelated context piling up.

  2) How do you reference a step after clearing?
  Point at the plan file path plus the step number, e.g.:

  ▎ "Implement step 1 (Fix C) from /home/vzell/.claude/plans/check-branch-filter-performance-fix-1-cheeky-blanket.md"

  The filename is a stable, unique slug auto-generated for this plan — it won't get overwritten by a future /plan run. Fresh session, no memory needed, just the path.

  3) Will the plan be stored anyway?
  Yes — it's already a real file on disk at that path (I wrote it with the Write/Edit tools, not just displayed it). It survives /clear, survives closing the terminal, survives indefinitely until deleted.

  4) Splitting steps across machines — how does the other machine know about the plan?
  This is the actual gap: ~/.claude/plans/ is local to this machine's home directory — it's not part of the git repo, so a second machine has no access to it at all. Three ways to fix that:

  - Copy the file over (scp, cloud drive, paste it) — simplest, but a manual step you'd have to remember each time you switch machines.
  - Commit it into the repo — you're already doing exactly this pattern: this very plan's original 3 questions are already sitting in README.org from the cd9a09d "add performance README" commit. I could append
  the findings/sizing table/step order there too, so git pull on the other machine gets it automatically.
  - Use the project's own established convention for this — CLAUDE.md already defines a feature-branch + <project>_CHANGELOG.wip.json workflow for exactly "work in progress that needs to survive across
  sessions/machines." Since each of the 5 steps is a natural standalone feature branch, doing steps 1-2 as commits on a branch and pushing it means the other machine just pulls that branch and has full context
  (code + WIP changelog) — no dependency on ~/.claude/plans at all.

  I'd recommend the last option since it's already your established pattern in this repo and travels via git automatically. Want me to append the step list to README.org (git-tracked) so it's portable, and/or
  set up the first feature branch for step 1? Note: I'm still in plan mode, so I can only touch the plan file right now — I'd need to exit plan mode to make repo edits.

✻ Worked for 44s

❯ should we remove the current performance fix branch

● My recommendation: don't delete it — rename/archive it instead.

  Reasoning:
  - The branch's commits are the actual reference implementation of the approach (the exact _artInitLazyPics IntersectionObserver logic, the show/hide pass replacing clone+re-render, the WIP changelog's own
  writeup of the bugs it hit and fixed along the way — e.g. the bigbox-filter-sync regression in WIP.3). Since we already established the idea is still valid but needs a fresh reimplementation against current
  main rather than a merge, that code is worth keeping as a blueprint to reference/port from, not just prose to remember.
  - Branches cost nothing to keep around in git. Deleting loses nothing today, but it's a one-way door if you ever want to diff against the old approach or copy a snippet (e.g. the observer setup) instead of
  rewriting it from scratch.
  - What actually needs to happen isn't "get rid of the branch," it's "make clear this branch won't be merged as-is." A rename communicates that without discarding anything:
  git branch -m filter-performance-fix archive/filter-performance-fix-v1-single-table
  - (and same on origin if you want it reflected there). That frees up a clean filter-performance-fix name for the actual redo, and the archive/ prefix signals "reference only, not mergeable" to future-you.

  If you do want it gone rather than archived, deleting a branch is exactly the kind of hard-to-reverse action I'd want explicit confirmation on before running — say the word and I'll do it (note: I'm still in
  plan mode right now, so I can't run either the rename or a delete until we're out of it).
#+end_example

Missing JSDoc: any exported/public function (call sites outside its own closure) or any non-trivial internal function (roughly: more than a couple of lines, or with non-obvious parameters) that has no doc block at all.
